# Interview P01: Regulatory and quality assurance lead at a medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** The participant is responsible for quality assurance and regulatory affairs at a medical-device manufacturer. She is the primary contact for certification activity with TUV SUD.
- **Workflow:** She initiates requests by email or phone, gathers internal information before contacting the auditor, maintains Appendix ABC in Excel, manages change/review cycles, and tracks project modules in a personal Excel database.
- **Goal:** Maintain accurate product and certification data while completing certification activities and financial closure predictably.
- **Reported concerns:** She describes Appendix ABC maintenance as "very tough" and revision realignment as "uncomfortable." She reports difficulty with billing closure. She considers a shared digital platform useful when it supports updates, process timing, and portfolio-level visibility.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "We start with the request by mail and then we send that to our auditor, lead auditor an application or change a notification and we complete all the documentation that she requests."
Code: #code/email-led-service-request

> "Actually we manage it with an Excel file file in our server and when they wrote it or depending on the project on the application request ask us to freeze the appendix."
Code: #code/versioned-excel-master-data

> "We create a subsequent revision of this appendix to manage the add of additional information going through time until the next freezing request from TUV SUD."
Code: #code/versioned-excel-master-data

> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "It is very tough because we have some thousands of code and then the number of devices is very high."
Code: #code/high-volume-product-data

> "We have an ERP, but ERP doesn't manage all the information that ABC then there is the equipment and the technical documentation."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Sometimes the seller, it's not possible to pass the copying code and pass the seller."
Code: #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel

> "We find some trouble in copy and paste the data from one to another file, not always being possible to edit the Excel."
Code: #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel

> "It's not clear for me when the process ends with the service cost invoice payment."
Code: #code/unclear-billing-closure

> "There are some delay in our invoice, and then our department, the account department is sometimes very in trouble for close relativity and all that."
Code: #code/unclear-billing-closure

> "Sometimes we didn't receive the support. It's a big problem because we didn't receive any answer or any support for using this kind of information."
Code: #code/unanswered-process-support

> "Personally, I maintain tracking of the approaches in an Excel file, signing the steps of the file."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "In this moment it's not work for all the project or for the whole activity."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "If the approaches are clear and follow all the steps of our certification project, I think it's very useful because it's a guide that helps us to fill all this information."
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "In this case, you can copy the product family information or you have to fill singularly each code?"
Code: #code/bulk-data-entry-needed

> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information."
Code: #code/bulk-data-entry-needed

> "With this kind of system we cannot have an overview and a summary of all the list of our devices with our devices with a list of all the study barrier sterilization process or main supplier."
Code: #code/portfolio-level-data-overview

> "In parallel way will be very useful to have also the system that if this information can put in a table or Excel file in order to see also the same view of appendix ABC of today."
Code: #code/portfolio-level-data-overview

> "With [our auditor], we are quite well informed about the information needed."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Theme Match

No existing theme notes were present in `02_themes` at the start of analysis. The following new themes are justified because the codes describe distinct, directly evidenced mechanisms rather than a generic dissatisfaction with the workflow:

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/versioned-excel-master-data; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/high-volume-product-data; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | New theme: no existing theme could capture the data-maintenance mechanism. |
| #code/revision-realignment-after-review | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | New theme: distinct review and version-control mechanism. |
| #code/unclear-process-timing; #code/personal-excel-process-tracking | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | New theme: distinct status and coverage mechanism. |
| #code/partial-platform-coverage | [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; this code describes partial platform coverage forcing channel switching, not status/timing opacity. |
| #code/unclear-billing-closure; #code/unanswered-process-support | [[Unclear service completion and invoice timing delays administrative closure]] | Reclassified: retain the two billing-closure quotes as a standalone preliminary pain point; the ambiguous support quote does not establish a cross-interview theme. |
| #code/bulk-data-entry-needed; #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: future-state requirement to enter data once and be guided through the process, kept separate from current pain mechanisms. |
| #code/portfolio-level-data-overview | [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]] | Direct confirmation: future-state requirement for a consolidated portfolio view, kept separate from current pain mechanisms. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | New positive theme: a working human-support pattern, not a pain point. |

## Topic Coverage Inventory

| Topic | Evidence / codes | Coverage decision | Artifact(s) | Gap / next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Appendix ABC maintenance | Excel server file, frozen Appendix, new revision, thousands of codes; `#code/versioned-excel-master-data`; `#code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance`; `#code/high-volume-product-data`; `#code/fragmented-product-data-sources` | Captured mechanism | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| Revision feedback and parallel work | TUV feedback arrives on a frozen file while the customer has an updated version; `#code/revision-realignment-after-review` | Captured mechanism | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]; [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] | None |
| Process timing and tracking | Step timing is unclear; participant tracks project steps in Excel; UCI does not cover all activity; `#code/unclear-process-timing`; `#code/personal-excel-process-tracking`; `#code/partial-platform-coverage` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]; [[Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step]] | None |
| Billing closure and invoice timing | Process end and invoice timing are unclear; accounting closure is delayed; `#code/unclear-billing-closure` | Preliminary mechanism | [[Unclear service completion and invoice timing delays administrative closure]] | Validate with other finance or administrative stakeholders. |
| Email-led request initiation | Requests start by email or phone to the auditor; `#code/email-led-service-request` | Related evidence | [[Customers need to submit certification requests before TUV creates a project]] | P01 does not state the later UCI project-creation gate directly. |
| Unanswered support | Participant reports missing support for process information; `#code/unanswered-process-support` | Research gap | None | Validate whether unanswered process support recurs and which process step it affects. |
| Named auditor guidance | The named auditor provides clear information requests and stays aligned with the activity; `#code/auditor-guidance-works` | Positive pattern | [[Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information]] | None |

## Reference
Analysis followed [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Steps 1-4. New codes require adding to [[Global Tags]] before the analysis is complete.

frontmatter.segment: Senior Regulatory Affairs Manager at a medical-device manufacturer

notes.body:
# Interview P02: Regulatory Affairs Manager at a medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** A Senior Regulatory Affairs Manager is the primary contact for certification work. She assembles technical documentation from subject-matter experts, submits it to TUV SUD, and is the sole UCI user on her side.
- **Workflow:** She submits applications through UCI, coordinates assessment scope and quotations, maintains a living Appendix ABC across MDR and MDSAP requirements, tracks projects and costs in Excel, and collaborates with TUV SUD through regular calls.
- **Goal:** Maintain accurate certification data, predict review scope and costs, and complete product changes without duplicated or error-prone administrative work.
- **Emotions and stance:** She describes Appendix ABC maintenance as a "huge effort," cost estimation as "extremely difficult," and unplanned assessment modules as a power imbalance. She values the recurring, transparent exchange with named TUV SUD contacts.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Ich hab mich dran gewöhnt, dass es nur via U.C.I. ist. Man kann gut darauf nachher referenzieren, wenn der Request mal liegen bleibt, dann schreib ich ein Mail."
>
> Translation: "I have become used to it only being via UCI. You can refer to it well afterwards; when the request is left pending, then I write an email."
Code: #code/request-follow-up-requires-email

> "Dort wissen wir ganz genau, was der Nodified Body pro Stunde verrechnet. Und dort wissen wir ganz genau, was ein Experte kostet und wie viel nachher der Experte für einen Review abgerechnet hat."
>
> Translation: "There, we know exactly what the notified body charges per hour. And we know exactly what an expert costs and how much the expert charged for a review."
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "Ich kann sie natürlich defenden, weil sie teilweise einfach nicht da ist zu einem Entwicklungsprojekt."
>
> Translation: "Of course, I can defend this because it is sometimes simply not available for a development project."
Code: #code/development-data-evolves

> "Nicht mal Appendix ABC von MDSAP und MDAR sind angeglichen."
>
> Translation: "Not even Appendix ABC for MDSAP and MDR are aligned."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel, weil ich brauche es ja eh, die Revision 09 vom MDR Appendix, weil der MDSAP Appendix brauch ich parallel jedes Jahr, weil der hat noch die ganzen Ablaufdaten hinten drin."
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel because I need revision 09 of the MDR Appendix anyway; I also need the MDSAP Appendix in parallel every year because it still contains all the expiry dates."
Code: #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions

> "Ich hab mit 2 geplant oder ups, war dann wirklich oder die Unterschiede, oder?"
>
> Translation: "I planned for two, then it suddenly became something else; the differences are enormous."
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg."
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."
Code: #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale

> "Das ist einfach, wo wir sicherlich ablegen, auch auch Dokumentation, zum Beispiel Deficiency Reports. Wo wir dran arbeiten können, die sind außerhalb vom DocuBridge."
>
> Translation: "That is simply where we store documentation as well, for example deficiency reports that we can work on; they are outside DocuBridge."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie? Wenn die Kosten umfangreicher sind und es Teilabrechnungen gibt, müssen wir das natürlich auch wissen, dass wir die Kosten tracken können."
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, when do they begin? When costs are larger and there are partial invoices, we also have to know that so we can track the costs."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "Das nicht jedes Mal ändern bei jeder Application."
>
> Translation: "Not having to change it every time for every application."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Da wird persönlich individuell benannt. Ja, ja, keine Chance."
>
> Translation: "It is named personally and individually. Yes, no chance."
Code: #code/document-organization-by-service

> "Was man nicht hat, ist den Request Progress. Der finde ich sehr transparent noch."
>
> Translation: "What one does not have is the request progress. I find that very transparent."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Für mich reicht eigentlich, wenn es so ist, theoretisch bei Udemed. Und von dem her, es muss keine Machine to Machine sein. Ich denke, mit Excel hochladen ist für uns vollkommen in Ordnung."
>
> Translation: "For me, it is enough if it is theoretically like EUDAMED. It does not have to be machine-to-machine. I think uploading Excel is completely fine for us."
Code: #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity

> "Was ist, wenn sich was ändert? Ich denk, das ist das größte Thema von allem. Wie merk ich das? Denk ich auch daran, dass ich dort auch noch was ändern muss, weil das wird jetzt immer signifikant schlimmer."
>
> Translation: "What happens when something changes? I think that is the biggest issue of all. How do I notice it? Do I also remember that I have to change something there, because it is becoming significantly worse now?"
Code: #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen."
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/personal-excel-process-tracking; #code/request-progress-visibility | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Direct confirmation: tracking and follow-up still require external tools; add P02 evidence and related pain points. |
| #code/request-follow-up-requires-email; #code/document-organization-by-service | [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; these codes describe channel/document consolidation, not status/timing opacity. |
| #code/development-data-evolves | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: data must be staged and entered only once it becomes available. |
| #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] | Direct confirmation: Excel upload is an acceptable channel and does not require a machine-to-machine interface. |
| #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data | [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] | Direct confirmation: distributed data must be actively maintained as it changes, which requires a reminder mechanism. |
| #code/misaligned-appendix-structures; #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | Direct confirmation: parallel structures and sources increase manual data-management burden. |
| #code/opaque-review-costs; #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale | [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]] | No existing theme fits the pre-quotation pricing and assessment-scope mechanism; create a new preliminary theme. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | Direct confirmation: regular, named contact supports transparency and should be retained. |
| #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale | [[Unclear service completion and invoice timing delays administrative closure]] | Related evidence only: assessment scoping precedes service closure and does not confirm this standalone pain point. |

notes.body:
# Interview P03: Quality Management System Manager at a medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** A Quality Management System Manager and ISO 13485 management representative at a medical-device manufacturer. She coordinates QMS changes, audits, and notified-body communication on quality-system matters, while Regulatory Affairs owns product-related communication.
- **Workflow:** QMS and Regulatory Affairs jointly prepare Appendix ABC from Oracle Fusion and other departmental sources; they anticipate changes in monthly calls, formalize them by email, manage evidence in SharePoint, and maintain separate Appendix ABC datasets for certification schemes and EUDAMED.
- **Goal:** Complete well-scoped changes without duplicate work, maintain accurate product and certificate information, and preserve traceable communication across personnel changes.
- **Emotions and stance:** She finds Appendix ABC difficult to maintain at the current portfolio scale, values monthly meetings highly, and describes repeated assessment or resubmission as double work.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "The Appendix ABC is really difficult to be maintained."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "We have one for the G15 for the ISO. And then we have the other for MDSAP."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "We have to fill in again all the information for all products."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "The solution of machine system that speak together will be the best solution."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "The solution that we can upload, for example, information like clinical supplier, we can upload our templates, could be a good compromise for me."
Code: #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information."
Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse

> "Maybe a common repository could be beneficial in order to work all on the same version."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on."
Code: #code/change-progresses-during-assessment

> "If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body."
Code: #code/incomplete-change-impact-assessment

> "The mistakes happen mostly due to communication. Because sometimes during a project, for example, during a change, some departments are not included."
Code: #code/cross-functional-change-impact-gaps

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Changes, assessment status, also deficiency status... timelines regarding the status, the expected closure date."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "I would prefer to have notification in order to be sure that there is a reminder, we are not missing anything."
Code: #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data

> "I would prefer to maintain the platform open just to few person in the company."
Code: #code/limited-platform-access

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/misaligned-appendix-structures | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | Direct confirmation: high-volume, manually updated, overlapping Appendix ABC datasets require duplicate maintenance. |
| #code/system-to-system-data-integration; #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] | Direct confirmation: a system-to-system interface is the ideal channel, with template upload as an accepted compromise. |
| #code/eudamed-data-reuse | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: data already available in EUDAMED should be reused rather than re-entered. |
| #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data | [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] | Direct confirmation: participants want a reminder so distributed changes are not missed. |
| #code/request-progress-visibility | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Direct confirmation: email-based history and scattered documentation make status and past decisions hard to retrieve. |
| #code/shared-certification-repository | [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; this code describes wanting one consolidated repository, not status/timing opacity. |
| #code/change-progresses-during-assessment | [[Long assessment intervals make submitted change documentation outdated]] | Standalone preliminary pain point: P03 reports internal change progress overtaking an active assessment; validate in another interview before creating a theme. |
| #code/incomplete-change-impact-assessment; #code/cross-functional-change-impact-gaps | [[Missing affected departments or assessments cause change resubmission]] | Standalone preliminary pain point: P03 reports a missed impact assessment that requires resubmission; validate in another interview before creating a theme. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | Direct confirmation: monthly discussions resolve uncertainty and sustain communication. |
| #code/limited-platform-access | [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] | Related pattern only: access governance is a platform constraint adjacent to shared-data governance; do not increase the theme's count or confidence from this code alone. |
| #code/change-progresses-during-assessment | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | Related pattern only: both involve asynchronous work, but P03 describes change progression during assessment rather than reconciling reviewer comments into a later revision. |

## Topic Coverage Inventory

| Topic | Evidence / codes | Coverage decision | Artifact(s) | Gap / next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Appendix ABC and scheme-specific data | Appendix is difficult to maintain; ISO and MDSAP data require duplicate entry; `#code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance`; `#code/fragmented-product-data-sources`; `#code/misaligned-appendix-structures` | Captured mechanism | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| Data reuse and repository | System-to-system connection, bulk upload, EUDAMED linkage, and common repository are desired; `#code/system-to-system-data-integration`; `#code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity`; `#code/eudamed-data-reuse`; `#code/shared-certification-repository` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]; [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]; [[Customers need to reuse European Database on Medical Devices (EUDAMED) product data]]; [[Customers need one place for certification status, documents, decisions, and messages]] | None |
| Change progress during assessment | Company changes continue while approval is pending; `#code/change-progresses-during-assessment` | Preliminary mechanism | [[Long assessment intervals make submitted change documentation outdated]] | Validate in another interview before theme or recommendation use. |
| Missed impact assessment | Missed assessment requires resubmission; departments can be omitted; `#code/incomplete-change-impact-assessment`; `#code/cross-functional-change-impact-gaps` | Preliminary mechanism | [[Missing affected departments or assessments cause change resubmission]] | Validate whether this repeats across other change coordinators. |
| Status, deficiency timing, and reminders | Participant wants assessment status, deficiency status, timelines, closure date, and reminders; `#code/request-progress-visibility`; `#code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]; [[Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step]]; [[Customers need reminders when product information changes in another system]] | None |
| Platform access | Platform access should remain limited to a few accountable people; `#code/limited-platform-access` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need scoped roles for viewing and changing certification data]] | None |
| Monthly clarification meetings | Monthly meetings clarify doubts and maintain communication; `#code/auditor-guidance-works` | Positive pattern | [[Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information]] | None |

## Reference

quotes.text: The Appendix ABC is really difficult to be maintained.
In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually.
We have one for the G15 for the ISO. And then we have the other for MDSAP.
We have to fill in again all the information for all products.
The solution of machine system that speak together will be the best solution.
The solution that we can upload, for example, information like clinical supplier, we can upload our templates, could be a good compromise for me.
If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information.
Maybe a common repository could be beneficial in order to work all on the same version.
Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on.
If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body.
The mistakes happen mostly due to communication. Because sometimes during a project, for example, during a change, some departments are not included.
The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication.
Changes, assessment status, also deficiency status... timelines regarding the status, the expected closure date.
I would prefer to have notification in order to be sure that there is a reminder, we are not missing anything.
I would prefer to maintain the platform open just to few person in the company.

notes.body:
# Interview P04: Regulatory Affairs specialists at a large medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** Two Regulatory Affairs specialists at a large manufacturer act as the notified-body interface for a broad portfolio. They prepare applications, maintain Appendix ABC, coordinate with Quality Management and Sterility Assurance, and use monthly and project-specific meetings with TUV SUD.
- **Workflow:** They submit clear cases by email with Appendix ABC changes, receive a UCI case after offer acceptance, and upload technical documentation there. Internally, they extract most data from Siemens Teamcenter and SAP, maintain a SharePoint working copy, and keep a separate reference-number appendix for high-volume certificates.
- **Goal:** Maintain one valid, traceable current data state while reducing manual transcription, version reconciliation, and the risk of mistakes across certification changes.
- **Reported concerns:** The participants describe Appendix ABC versioning as "very, very difficult." They report that manual reconciliation requires substantial effort. They report that improved UCI status information and recurring meetings with TUV contacts support their work.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Ich glaube auch im im U.C.I. Tool sind ja die Slots mit hinterlegt. Das das hilft."
>
> Translation: "I think the slots are also stored in the UCI tool. That helps."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz."
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch."
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export."
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Die Versionierung ist sehr, sehr schwierig."
>
> Translation: "Versioning is very, very difficult."
Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon."
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."
Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Es ist natürlich bei, ich weiß nicht wie viel Datenpunkten, sehr, sehr, sehr mühsam, das dann manuell nachzupflegen."
>
> Translation: "With I do not know how many data points, it is of course very, very, very laborious to manually carry that forward."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Das Hin und Hergeklicke, das stimmt."
>
> Translation: "All the clicking back and forth, that is true."
Code: #code/cross-tab-data-navigation

> "Die eingeschränkten Rechte, also dass ich nicht Zeilen hinzufügen kann oder löschen kann."
>
> Translation: "The restricted permissions, meaning that I cannot add or delete rows."
Code: #code/restricted-row-editing

> "Ich reich die zwar ein, dass ich sie für mich, aber danach geht es doch immer alles nach einer TÜV-Projektliste."
>
> Translation: "I submit it so that I have it for myself, but afterwards everything proceeds according to a TUV project list."
Code: #code/customer-change-id-not-retained

> "Dann habe ich parallel eben die Arbeitsversion V24."
>
> Translation: "Then I have the working version V24 running in parallel."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Ein Portal, ein Zugang, also ein Endprodukt oder wie auch immer man es nennen will."
>
> Translation: "One portal, one access point, an end product, or whatever one wants to call it."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion."
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."
Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

> "Wenn mein Supplier 'n TÜV-Süd Zertifikat habt, dass ihr euch das selber zieht. Ihr habt es schließlich auch ausgestellt."
>
> Translation: "When my supplier has a TUV SUD certificate, you should retrieve it yourselves. After all, you issued it."
Code: #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates

> "Wir haben 'nen ungefähr 'nen monatlichen Call, wo aber dann auch Quality Sterility Assurance dabei ist, wo unsere offenen Themen besprochen werden."
>
> Translation: "We have an approximately monthly call that also includes Quality and Sterility Assurance, where our open topics are discussed."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision; #code/revision-realignment-after-review | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | Direct confirmation: multiple concurrent Appendix states require manual comparison and carry-forward work. |
| #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/cross-tab-data-navigation; #code/restricted-row-editing | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | Direct confirmation: manual list production, navigation across dependent tabs, and fixed row structures increase error risk and effort. |
| #code/system-to-system-data-integration; #code/automated-data-validity-checks | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] | Direct confirmation: data should be exchanged from a leading system through a defined interface and validated automatically. |
| #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: certificates TUV SUD already issued to a supplier should be reused rather than re-collected from the customer. |
| #code/request-progress-visibility; #code/unclear-process-timing; #code/customer-change-id-not-retained | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Direct confirmation: UCI status has improved, but certificate timing and traceability from customer change IDs through project correspondence remain insufficient. |
| #code/shared-certification-repository | [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; this code describes wanting one consolidated repository, not status/timing opacity. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | Direct confirmation: cross-functional monthly calls provide valuable proactive coordination. |
| #code/restricted-row-editing | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | Related pattern only: editing restrictions contribute to version-management difficulty but are a distinct template constraint; do not increase interview count based on this code alone. |

## Topic Coverage Inventory

| Topic | Evidence / codes | Coverage decision | Artifact(s) | Gap / next check |

| UCI slots and certificate timing | UCI slots help, but certificate timing remains unclear; `#code/request-progress-visibility`; `#code/unclear-process-timing` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]; [[Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step]] | None |
| Fragmented product data and interfaces | Product data come from source systems and should be exported through an interface; `#code/fragmented-product-data-sources`; `#code/system-to-system-data-integration` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| Appendix version collisions and carry-forward | Multiple Appendix versions arrive concurrently and must be manually carried forward; `#code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision`; `#code/revision-realignment-after-review` | Captured mechanism | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]; [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] | None |
| Template restrictions | Users cannot add or delete rows; `#code/restricted-row-editing` | Related evidence | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]; [[Fixed Appendix rows require separate reference lists]] | Captured through fixed-row and Appendix-maintenance mechanisms. |
| Customer change identifier | Customer-side change notification disappears into TUV project lists; `#code/customer-change-id-not-retained` | Captured mechanism | [[Customer change-notification IDs are lost across TUV correspondence and billing]]; [[Customers need their change-notification ID retained through the TUV process]] | None |
| Data checks and supplier certificate reuse | Customer wants automatic validity checks and reuse of TUV-issued supplier certificates; `#code/automated-data-validity-checks`; `#code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need automatic certification-data checks and reminders for missing information]]; [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]; [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | None |
| Monthly cross-functional TUV call | Monthly calls include Quality and Sterility Assurance; `#code/auditor-guidance-works` | Positive pattern | [[Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information]] | None |

## Reference

notes.body:
# Interview P05: Regulatory Affairs managers at a large medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** Two experienced Regulatory Affairs managers at a large manufacturer manage MDR remediation, Class III device maintenance, renewals, and notified-body communication for separate operating units.
- **Workflow:** They initiate work through recurring meetings or email, submit applications and Appendix ABC updates, manage high-volume product and supplier metadata from distributed systems, and use UCI to differing degrees depending on regional onboarding and device class.
- **Goal:** Maintain correct product and supplier data, understand the certification timeline through final certification-body review, and avoid missed review actions while retaining direct working relationships with TUV contacts.
- **Emotions and stance:** They describe Excel maintenance and synchronization as a heavy manual burden. They welcome a digital system but explicitly want it to complement, not replace, personal communication.

## Meaning Units and Codes

notes.body:
# Interview P06: Regulatory Affairs leaders at a medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participants and setting:** A Director of Regulatory Affairs, a CE Regulatory Affairs team lead, and a regulatory-requirements specialist at a medical-device manufacturer describe how a 25-person department manages MDR and MDSAP Appendix ABC activity alongside global registrations.
- **Workflow:** The team submits most requests through UCI, maintains controlled Appendix ABC versions in its document-management system, consolidates product and supplier data from PLM, other internal systems, EUDAMED, and country-specific databases, then tracks submissions internally when UCI status is not current enough.
- **Goal:** Submit the right information once, understand what each service request requires, maintain a reliable current record, and see whether TUV has received, reviewed, or accepted the submission.
- **Emotions and stance:** Participants regard the current Excel work as costly, repetitive, and error-prone, while also reporting responsive personal support. They want contextual guidance and validation, not a long static manual or excessive notifications.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Das ist beim TÜV Süd auch 'ne Excel-Liste, wo halt aus meiner Sicht 'ne Tabellenkalkulationssoftware verwendet wurde, um 'ne Datenbank aufzubauen. Ist aus meiner Richtung nicht gut geeignet."
>
> Translation: "At TUV SUD it is also an Excel list where, from my perspective, a spreadsheet application is being used to build a database. From my perspective, it is not well suited."
Code: #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel

> "Wir haben halt auch immer so, sag ich mal, doppelt und dreifach Pflege, weil jemand muss es ja auch in die Health Canada Datenbank eintragen, dann müssen wir es noch mal in das Appendix A. B. C. eintragen und dann noch mal in unser System eintragen."
>
> Translation: "We also always have double and triple maintenance, because someone has to enter it in the Health Canada database, then we have to enter it again in Appendix ABC, and then again in our system."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Im Moment machen wir alles über das U.C.I. Portal."
>
> Translation: "At the moment, we do everything through the UCI portal."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen."
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren."
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Aber da hatte ich bei den Produkten schon einiges ausgefüllt gehabt, wo dann der [unser TUV-Kontakt] gesagt hat, nee, wenn ich das so und so angebe, müssen Sie die und die Prüfung machen, weil es ja so nicht richtig ist."
>
> Translation: "I had already completed quite a few product entries where [our TUV contact] said that if I specify it this way, you have to perform certain assessments because it is not correct that way."
Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten."
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Und deswegen sind wir dann hergegangen und haben quasi 'ne eigene Übersicht gemacht, wo wir eigentlich die gleichen Informationen nehmen und etwas detaillierter noch beschreiben, damit wir damit klarkommen und dann intern quasi auch kommunizieren können."
>
> Translation: "That is why we created our own overview, using essentially the same information but describing it in more detail so we can manage it and communicate internally."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam."
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."
Code: #code/high-volume-product-data

> "Ich fänd es besser, wenn es eben nicht übers U.C.I. Portal gehen würde, sondern über 'ne definierte Schnittstelle, dass eben, ich sag mal in Realtime, ab dem Zeitpunkt, wo ich auf den Knopf drück, jetzt bitte senden, dass dann die Daten übertragen werden."
>
> Translation: "I would prefer it not to go through the UCI portal but through a defined interface, so that in real time, from the moment I press send, the data are transferred."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden."
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."
Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung."
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Wenn ich jetzt eine Neuproduktanmeldung habe, was brauchen Sie dafür noch mit dazu, reicht da nur die IFQ, wollen Sie da gleich Broschüren haben oder sonstige Informationen?"
>
> Translation: "If I have a new product registration, what else do you need for it? Is the IFQ enough, or do you also want brochures or other information?"
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen."
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Ich kenn es schon aus der Vergangenheit bei anderen Unternehmen, wenn ich von den Systemen so viele Bling und Bings und hier ist was geschehen und hier ist was geschehen, dann habe ich also schon mehrfach überlegt, da gibt es so 'n Overflow und was passiert, keiner erfasst die Sachen mehr, weil es zu viel Bling, Bling und Bing und Bang ist."
>
> Translation: "I know from the past at other companies that when systems produce so many pings and notifications that something happened, there is an overflow and nobody notices things anymore because there is too much pinging."
Code: #code/critical-uci-notification-missed

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/high-volume-product-data | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | Direct confirmation: Excel is treated as an unsuitable database, repeated entry spans several external and internal systems, and large lists become slow and error-prone. |
| #code/revision-realignment-after-review | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | Direct confirmation: TUV-created versions must be downloaded, re-versioned, and returned to the internal controlled-document workflow. |
| #code/request-progress-visibility; #code/personal-excel-process-tracking | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Direct confirmation: an outdated UCI overview leads to an internal tracker; participants need receipt/review confirmation but caution against high-volume notifications. |
| #code/critical-uci-notification-missed | [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; this code describes wanting a review-acknowledgement alert, not status/timing opacity. |
| #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow; #code/eudamed-data-reuse | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: a future workflow should use conditional, guided fields and reuse EUDAMED data rather than static forms and repeated manual entry. |
| #code/system-to-system-data-integration; #code/automated-data-validity-checks | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] | Direct confirmation: a defined system interface with automated validation is preferred over the current portal-based entry. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | Direct confirmation: responsive project meetings and direct questions provide effective guidance today. |
| #code/critical-uci-notification-missed | [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] | Related evidence: the participant warns that notification overload can make important changes invisible, reinforcing the existing alert-design implication without creating a separate theme. |

## Topic Coverage Inventory

| Topic | Evidence / codes | Coverage decision | Artifact(s) | Gap / next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Excel as database and repeated entry | Appendix ABC is a spreadsheet used as a database; Health Canada, Appendix ABC, and internal systems duplicate work; `#code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel`; `#code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance`; `#code/high-volume-product-data` | Captured mechanism | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| Interfaces and EUDAMED | Participant wants defined real-time transfer and EUDAMED reuse; `#code/system-to-system-data-integration`; `#code/eudamed-data-reuse` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need to reuse European Database on Medical Devices (EUDAMED) product data]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| Controlled-document re-versioning | TUV-created versions must be downloaded and re-versioned internally; `#code/revision-realignment-after-review` | Captured mechanism | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]; [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] | None |
| UCI overview and internal tracker | UCI overview is useful but not transparent or current enough; internal overview duplicates it; `#code/request-progress-visibility`; `#code/personal-excel-process-tracking` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]; [[Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step]] | None |
| Receipt and review confirmation | Participant wants status that TUV saw and reviewed entries; `#code/request-progress-visibility` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need confirmation when TUV receives or reviews a submission]] | None |
| Guidance and validation | Users want conditional guidance for required fields/documents and formal pre-checks; `#code/guided-end-to-end-workflow`; `#code/automated-data-validity-checks` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need the required fields and documents for each selected service]]; [[Customers need automatic certification-data checks and reminders for missing information]] | None |
| Notification overload | Too many system pings can make important information invisible; `#code/critical-uci-notification-missed` | Related evidence | [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] | Retain as alert-design evidence unless action-required alerts are missed. |
| Responsive TUV support | Project meetings and questions receive fast responses; `#code/auditor-guidance-works` | Positive pattern | [[Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information]] | None |

> "Wir haben halt auch immer so, sag ich mal, doppelt und dreifach Pflege, weil jemand muss es ja auch in die Health Canada Datenbank eintragen, dann müssen wir es noch mal in das Appendix A. B. C. eintragen und dann noch mal in unser System eintragen."
>
> Translation: "We also always have double and triple maintenance, because someone has to enter it in the Health Canada database, then we have to enter it again in Appendix ABC, and then again in our system."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Im Moment machen wir alles über das U.C.I. Portal."
>
> Translation: "At the moment, we do everything through the UCI portal."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen."
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren."
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Aber da hatte ich bei den Produkten schon einiges ausgefüllt gehabt, wo dann der [unser TUV-Kontakt] gesagt hat, nee, wenn ich das so und so angebe, müssen Sie die und die Prüfung machen, weil es ja so nicht richtig ist."
>
> Translation: "I had already completed quite a few product entries where [our TUV contact] said that if I specify it this way, you have to perform certain assessments because it is not correct that way."
Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten."
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Und deswegen sind wir dann hergegangen und haben quasi 'ne eigene Übersicht gemacht, wo wir eigentlich die gleichen Informationen nehmen und etwas detaillierter noch beschreiben, damit wir damit klarkommen und dann intern quasi auch kommunizieren können."
>
> Translation: "That is why we created our own overview, using essentially the same information but describing it in more detail so we can manage it and communicate internally."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam."
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."
Code: #code/high-volume-product-data

> "Ich fänd es besser, wenn es eben nicht übers U.C.I. Portal gehen würde, sondern über 'ne definierte Schnittstelle, dass eben, ich sag mal in Realtime, ab dem Zeitpunkt, wo ich auf den Knopf drück, jetzt bitte senden, dass dann die Daten übertragen werden."
>
> Translation: "I would prefer it not to go through the UCI portal but through a defined interface, so that in real time, from the moment I press send, the data are transferred."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden."
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."
Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung."
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Wenn ich jetzt eine Neuproduktanmeldung habe, was brauchen Sie dafür noch mit dazu, reicht da nur die IFQ, wollen Sie da gleich Broschüren haben oder sonstige Informationen?"
>
> Translation: "If I have a new product registration, what else do you need for it? Is the IFQ enough, or do you also want brochures or other information?"
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen."
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Ich kenn es schon aus der Vergangenheit bei anderen Unternehmen, wenn ich von den Systemen so viele Bling und Bings und hier ist was geschehen und hier ist was geschehen, dann habe ich also schon mehrfach überlegt, da gibt es so 'n Overflow und was passiert, keiner erfasst die Sachen mehr, weil es zu viel Bling, Bling und Bing und Bang ist."
>
> Translation: "I know from the past at other companies that when systems produce so many pings and notifications that something happened, there is an overflow and nobody notices things anymore because there is too much pinging."
Code: #code/critical-uci-notification-missed

notes.title: Interview P07: Quality Management System lead at a medical-device manufacturer

frontmatter.segment: Quality Management System lead at a medical-device manufacturer

notes.body:
# Interview P07: Quality Management System lead at a medical-device manufacturer

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** The participant leads the Quality Management System team at a medical-device manufacturer. Regulatory Affairs manages product-specific changes and device lists, while her team manages applications, audits, certificates, and QMS-related change notifications.
- **Workflow:** The team coordinates open items and ongoing changes in a shared Excel file and triweekly calls with named TUV contacts. It maintains controlled Appendix files alongside product, supplier, and technical information held in Windchill, Polarion, SAP, EUDAMED, and national databases.
- **Goal:** Supply current structured data once, preserve controlled manufacturer records, see notified-body review outcomes, and make change, audit, certification, and budget decisions with predictable timing and rationale.
- **Emotions and stance:** The participant values the established human collaboration but describes the Appendix as the most painful source of manual work. She is open to joint digital workflows if ownership, roles, auditability, and technical interfaces are explicit.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut."
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Also es läuft aktuell sehr viel parallel zwischen E-Mail und UCI Portal."
>
> Translation: "Currently, a great deal runs in parallel between email and the UCI portal."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen."
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Supply-Informationen haben wir wiederum in anderen Datenbanken, das pflegen wir in S.A.P., das heißt, das müssen wir separat rausziehen."
>
> Translation: "We have supply information in other databases, maintained in SAP, which means we have to extract it separately."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Oft ist es ja so, dass wenn man 'ne Change Notification einreicht, dass zu dem Zeitpunkt die Details, die in den Appendix eingetragen werden müssen, noch nicht klar sind, auch noch nicht vonnöten sind."
>
> Translation: "When submitting a change notification, the details that must be entered in the Appendix are often not yet clear or needed at that time."
Code: #code/development-data-evolves

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History."
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."
Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail

> "Wir haben zum Beispiel dieses Jahr im Audit erlebt, dass die Auditoren in einer Version vom Appendix A. B. C. nachgeschaut haben, die total outdated war."
>
> Translation: "This year during the audit, the auditors reviewed a version of Appendix ABC that was completely outdated."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?"
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen."
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind."
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist."
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Also das ist natürlich extrem unpraktisch."
>
> Translation: "That is, of course, extremely impractical."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?"
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht."
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."
Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "Was da drin steht, gehört zu uns."
>
> Translation: "What is in it belongs to us."
Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "In der Datenbank könnte ich mir ja gut vorstellen, dass man das über Status abfangen kann. Also Entered by Manufacturer, Reviewed by Notified Body, Feedback by Notified Body oder so."
>
> Translation: "In a database, I could imagine handling this through statuses: entered by manufacturer, reviewed by notified body, feedback by notified body, or similar."
Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/misaligned-appendix-structures | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | Direct confirmation: separate controlled files and distributed source systems require repeated manual maintenance and reconciliation. |
| #code/revision-realignment-after-review; #code/shared-data-audit-trail | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | Direct confirmation: reviewer changes must be manually transferred back into a controlled customer record because the shared process has no audit trail or field-level review states. |
| #code/unclear-process-timing | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Direct confirmation: UCI and email run in parallel, and audit submission timing is unclear enough that auditors can use an outdated Appendix version. |
| #code/partial-platform-coverage | [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; this code describes email/UCI channel parallelism, not status/timing opacity. |
| #code/system-to-system-data-integration | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] | Direct confirmation: a future interface needs structured, digital exchange rather than manual re-entry. |
| #code/development-data-evolves | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: data become available at different stages and should be entered as they become ready. |
| #code/role-based-data-governance | [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] | Direct confirmation: a future interface needs scoped contributor, reviewer, and approver roles. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | Direct confirmation: triweekly shared-topic meetings with named contacts are an effective current working pattern. |
| #code/opaque-review-costs | [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]] | Direct confirmation: unexplained cost increases undermine budget planning and require repeated follow-up for rationale. |

## Topic Coverage Inventory

| Topic | Evidence / codes | Coverage decision | Artifact(s) | Gap / next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parallel email and UCI work | Communication runs in parallel across email and UCI; `#code/partial-platform-coverage` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]; [[Customers need one place for certification status, documents, decisions, and messages]] | None |
| Audit timing and outdated Appendix use | Auditors used an outdated Appendix version; participant is unsure whether to submit proactively before audits; `#code/unclear-process-timing` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Captured under timing and stale-data use, not a separate audit theme. |
| Distributed product and supplier data | Product and supplier data sit in Windchill, Polarion, SAP, EUDAMED, and national databases; `#code/system-to-system-data-integration`; `#code/fragmented-product-data-sources` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| Development-stage data | Appendix details may not be known or needed at change-notification time; `#code/development-data-evolves` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need to add product information when it becomes available]] | None |
| Audit trail and review statuses | There is no audit trail; database statuses could show entered, reviewed, and feedback states; `#code/shared-data-audit-trail` | Captured mechanism | [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]]; [[Customers need field-level history for shared data changes and review actions]] | None |
| Role-based ownership | Manufacturer owns its data and may need approver roles; `#code/role-based-data-governance` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need scoped roles for viewing and changing certification data]] | None |
| Cost increase rationale | Cost increases arrive without explanation; `#code/opaque-review-costs` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]]; [[Customers need quotation cost components and assessment-module rationale before acceptance]] | None |
| Triweekly coordination | Shared Excel and triweekly meetings work well; `#code/auditor-guidance-works` | Positive pattern | [[Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information]] | None |

## Reference
Analysis followed [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Steps 1-4. New P07 codes are registered in [[Global Tags]].

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?"
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen."
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind."
>

Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist."
>

Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Also das ist natürlich extrem unpraktisch."
>

Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?"
>

> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht."
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."
Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "Was da drin steht, gehört zu uns."
>
> Translation: "What is in it belongs to us."
Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "In der Datenbank könnte ich mir ja gut vorstellen, dass man das über Status abfangen kann. Also Entered by Manufacturer, Reviewed by Notified Body, Feedback by Notified Body oder so."
>
> Translation: "In a database, I could imagine handling this through statuses: entered by manufacturer, reviewed by notified body, feedback by notified body, or similar."
Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail
