sections.Context:
- **Participants:** A Senior Director Quality and Regulatory Global Operations and IT, and a Director Quality Management, at a global medical-device manufacturer.
- **Workflow:** The leaders coordinate notified-body communication, significant changes, certification projects, quotations, Appendix ABC data, audits, and quality-system documentation across a global group.
- **Goal:** Retain access to trusted human contacts while replacing document and channel switches with a guided, traceable platform that reuses shared data, shows ownership and milestones, and minimizes formal rework.
- **Observed sentiment:** Participants value long-standing TUV support and do not describe routine project setup as time-critical, but identify avoidable manual data re-entry, version uncertainty, fragmented request initiation, opaque task ownership, and PDF-based interaction as unnecessary effort.
sections.Transcript in Meaning Units:
> "UCI nutzen wir. Ja, ist okay. Allerdings muss man ja immer zuerst in U.C.I. muss ja ein Projekt eröffnet werden, bevor man dann irgendwas übermitteln kann, selbst wenn ich jetzt 'ne neue Anfrage hatte, 'ne Significant Change oder so, die kann ich, ich persönlich oder als Kunde kann ich im U.C.I. nicht draufklicken, mach mir was Neues auf und füll das dann da drin an."
>
> Translation: "We use UCI. It is okay. However, a project must first be opened in UCI before you can submit anything; even when I have a new request or a significant change, I personally, as the customer, cannot click in UCI, create a new item, and complete it there."
>
> Code: #code/customer-cannot-initiate-platform-request

> "Also ich hätte es eher so vielleicht als Thema, warum wir es angesprochen haben, so als Medienwechsel oder sowas genannt. Ja, also digital Papier, Telefon besprechen, Teams, weiß ich nicht. Da sind halt sehr viele Brüche drin."
>
> Translation: "I would describe it more as media changes: digital, paper, discussing by phone, Teams. There are many breaks in between."
>
> Code: #code/multiple-channel-context-switching

> "In der idealen Welt und wir haben das bei Projekten ja auch bei Prozessen bei uns auch so, wenn sie nur in einem System arbeiten müssen, wenn sie das komplett einmal keine PDFs ausfüllen müssen, keine irgendwie Anträge machen müssen, also wenn es dann in einem System funktionieren könnte."
>
> Translation: "In an ideal world, you only have to work in one system and do not have to complete PDFs or separate application forms; it would work in one system."
>
> Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Wenn ich sage, nein, wünscht ihr was, dann habe ich 'ne Plattform, heißt die U.C.I. oder wie auch immer und ich logge mich ein und sage, ich mache 'ne new Application und dann wähle ich aus, will ich jetzt mein Ist es produktbezogen, ist es QM-System bezogen und ich habe eine gewisse Logik dahinter und ich werde dementsprechend durchgeführt."
>
> Translation: "If I could wish for it, I would have a platform where I log in, create a new application, choose whether it concerns a product or the quality-management system, and am guided by the appropriate logic."
>
> Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Dann sehe ich halt eine Notification. Die kann ich aber heute nicht gefühlt nicht als gelesen aktivieren. Die muss ich mir runterladen. Die will ich aber gar nicht runterladen."
>
> Translation: "Then I see a notification. At present, I do not feel that I can mark it as read. I have to download it, although I do not want to download it."
>
> Code: #code/notification-read-state-requires-download

> "Das kann ich aber nicht eintragen, weil das PDF digital signiert ist vom TÜV. Das kann ich nicht ändern. Das kann ich aber auch nicht als PDF drucken. Das muss ich ausdrucken und scannen."
>
> Translation: "I cannot enter that because the PDF is digitally signed by TUV. I cannot change it, nor can I print it as a PDF. I have to print and scan it."
>
> Code: #code/pdf-signature-forces-print-scan

> "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. fürs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prüfung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prüfung, das ist O.K. Ich wüsste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen könnte in der Übersicht. Das wäre ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TÜV. Das sieht man primär nicht."
>
> Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; [the manufacturer] owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."
>
> Code: #code/task-ownership-not-visible

> "Aber sagen wir mal, die Zwischendinger die Zwischenmeilensteine, die sieht man jetzt aktuell nicht in der Übersicht, wo du sagst, okay, der TÜV antwortet bis dahin oder wir müssen dann bis 90 Tage danach oder was auch immer dann ein Feedback geben, dass man sowas auch in der Übersicht sieht."
>
> Translation: "The intermediate milestones are not currently visible in the overview, such as when TUV will respond or when we must give feedback within 90 days."
>
> Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Ja, was S.C.N. angeht, da haben wir 'ne 'ne Liste, klassisch, also das sind viele, das sind vielleicht 'n paar im Jahr, ist 'ne klassische Excel-Liste, wo wir sagen, O.K., was sind die Dokumente, die wir eingereicht haben, wir haben bei uns im SharePoint dann noch organisiert."
>
> Translation: "For significant change notifications, we use a traditional Excel list to record the documents we submitted, organized in SharePoint."
>
> Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "Das, das, das, das meiste ist, glaube ich, dass man alles wieder neu eintragen muss, ja, weil sich ja gefühlt alle drei Wochen die Version oder Revision."
>
> Translation: "The main issue is that you have to enter everything again because it feels as though the version or revision changes every three weeks."
>
> Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance, #code/versioned-excel-master-data

> "Was auch schwierig war, dass die unterschiedlich aufgebaut sind, gerade MDR, MDD, unterschiedliche auch Nomenklaturen teilweise verwendet wurden."
>
> Translation: "It was also difficult that they are structured differently, especially MDR and MDD, and sometimes use different nomenclatures."
>
> Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "Man muss eigentlich jede Zeile, jede Spalte, jede Zelle angucken, was man da jetzt wirklich eintragen muss."
>
> Translation: "You essentially have to look at every row, every column, and every cell to determine what must be entered."
>
> Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Da wäre wirklich 'n keine Ahnung. Ich kann nicht mehr 'ne Datenbank, bei die im System ist, irgendwie schon einfacher vorstellen, wenn man sagt, O.K., man man fangt an zu tippen und dann kommen schon die Auswahlfelder, was man eingeben kann. und dann ist es immer das gleiche Format und immer das gleiche."
>
> Translation: "A database in the system would be easier: you start typing, select from available options, and always use the same format."
>
> Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks, #code/editable-structured-records

> "Gefühlt immer. Also ich warte immer, bis ich den letzten kriege."
>
> Translation: "It feels like it happens all the time. I always wait until I receive the latest version."
>
> Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Wenn wir Änderungen machen, dann sagen wir: 'Führ das bitte zusammen und schick mir die dann.' Das dauert aber dann auch."
>
> Translation: "When we make changes, we say: please consolidate it and then send it to me. But that also takes time."
>
> Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Meiner Meinung nach hat der Hersteller die Datenhoheit, weil es unsere Daten sind."
>
> Translation: "In my opinion, the manufacturer has data sovereignty because they are our data."
>
> Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "Dann unter Umständen, wenn es unsere Daten sind, dann vielleicht irgendeine Acknowledgement-Genehmigung oder sonst irgendwas."
>
> Translation: "When it is our data, there should perhaps be some acknowledgement or approval."
>
> Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "Wenn jetzt die Schnittstelle ein Standardformat ist, das wäre natürlich sehr gut."
>
> Translation: "If the interface used a standard format, that would naturally be very good."
>
> Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Aktuell ist es schon eher Distrib, also verteilt, verteilte Daten."
>
> Translation: "At present, the data are distributed across different places."
>
> Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Aber für sollte jetzt da 'ne Anbindung aus U.C.I. oder einem neuen Datenbank oder wie auch immer an Eudamed möglich sein, halte ich das für durchaus sinnvoll."
>
> Translation: "If a connection from UCI, a new database, or whatever form it takes to EUDAMED becomes possible, I consider that entirely sensible."
>
> Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse

> "Wie gesagt, so gut es geht digital zu haben, kein PDF mehr ausdrucken zu müssen, um irgendwas reinzugeben und dann ist digital zu unterschreiben, wie auch immer das da der Austausch da ist."
>
> Translation: "As far as possible, it should be digital: no more printing PDFs to enter something and then signing digitally."
>
> Code: #code/editable-structured-records

> "Wenn sagen wir mal Deficiencies sind oder auch Findings, die auch digital in einem Tool beantworten zu können, ohne Dokumente auszufüllen."
>
> Translation: "Deficiencies or findings should be answerable digitally in one tool without completing documents."
>
> Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Ich möchte meinen Project Handler oder meinen Relationship Manager, wie auch immer, rein. Nicht dass ich zuerst durch muss und sitz dann wie gefühlt die 10 Minuten in der Warteschlange."
>
> Translation: "I want to bring in my project handler or relationship manager, rather than first having to go through a process and wait in a queue for ten minutes."
>
> Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Dass man da in gewisser Art und Weise und ich weiß, ihr habt dann betrifft darf ja dann auch nicht beraten, aber gibt es dann so eine Art Vorprüfung oder sonst irgendwas? Geht es in die Richtung, wo ich mir wünschen würde, als Kunde vielleicht dazu sagen, ich schicke das einfach mal zum Check ein und es läuft durch und gibt mir dann die formalen Punkte."
>
> Translation: "Could there be some kind of preliminary check? I would like to submit something for a check and have it identify the formal issues."
>
> Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

notes.body:
# Interview P11: Regulatory Affairs team at a medical-device manufacturer

## Context
- **Participants:** A Regulatory Affairs team lead and two Regulatory Affairs specialists at a medical-device manufacturer.
- **Workflow:** The team maintains three Appendix ABC variants, prepares applications and change notifications, coordinates product and supplier data from SAP and technical documentation, and exchanges certification information through UCI, files, and named contacts.
- **Goal:** Maintain a controlled, traceable shared certification record without copying the same data and document versions across projects, while preserving regulatory approval gates and human accountability.
- **Observed sentiment:** Participants describe UCI project work and TUV-provided template migration as useful, but the current Excel and PDF workflow creates repeated copying, version risk, formatting work, and local PDF workarounds.

## Transcript in Meaning Units

> "Wir mussen 3 Appendixe pflegen, es sind viele redundante Daten und auch beim Upload in U. C. I. haben wir immer mal wieder das Problem, dass wir immer doppelt uploaden mussen."
>
> Translation: "We have to maintain three appendices with much redundant data, and when uploading to UCI we repeatedly have the problem that we must upload twice."
>
> Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen."
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."
>
> Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Wir haben immer eine offene Draftversion, da wird fleissig eingetragen, was so kommt, bis der Tag kommt, wo so, jetzt mussen wir mal ein Update schicken."
>
> Translation: "We always have an open draft version where changes are entered until the day comes when we must send an update."
>
> Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Wenn wir das itembasiert oder produktbasiert updaten konnten, das ware, glaube ich, schon mal unheimlich hilfreich."
>
> Translation: "If we could update it by item or product, that would be extremely helpful."
>
> Code: #code/editable-structured-records

> "Diese ganzen Daten stehen bei uns mal unabhangig von S. A. P. Sie stehen ja naturlich irgendwo in der technischen Akte, aber sagen wir mal in 3, 4, 5 verschiedenen Dokumenten."
>
> Translation: "All these data exist independently of SAP; they are somewhere in the technical documentation, in perhaps three, four, or five different documents."
>
> Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Wir mussen das ja erst mal bei euch anmelden und durfen ja auch nicht implementieren, bevor das approved ist."
>
> Translation: "We first have to notify you and are not allowed to implement it before it is approved."
>
> Code: #code/regulatory-approval-gates-data-synchronization

> "Dann haben wir auch die Problematik, jetzt haben wir acht Tandems, acht Produktgruppen, die haben nicht immer was."
>
> Translation: "We also have the issue that we have eight pairs and eight product groups, which do not always have something to work on."
>
> Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Wenn Sie einen neuen Supplier zum Beispiel eintragen, machen Sie die ganze neue Zeile gelb oder wenn Sie in irgendeiner Zelle was andern, machen Sie die Zelle gelb und schreiben mir vorne in der History auch recht ausfuhrlich gerne immer hin, was haben Sie denn gemacht und warum."
>
> Translation: "When they enter a new supplier, for example, they highlight the entire new row in yellow; when they change a cell, they highlight that cell and write in the history what they changed and why."
>
> Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches."
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."
>
> Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail

> "Wenn ich jetzt bei einem den Eintrag eher fuge einen E. R. C. Code fur diese Seite hinzu und wenn da jetzt ein Icon ware, Information, Achtung, ERC Codes, blablabla, einfach so ein bisschen und ein paar Links, ja klar, ware naturlich immer toll."
>
> Translation: "If I add an ERC code for a site, it would be helpful to have an information icon with guidance and links about ERC codes."
>
> Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer."
>
> Translation: "The main pain points at present are that we have to maintain three appendices, in whatever form."
>
> Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures, #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Online naturlich einfacher ware, ihr wollt ein neues Item haben und dann ploppt bei uns auf 'Bitte nachpflegen' und dann scrollen wir uns einfach durch pro Produkt oder pro Supplier und pflegen dieses eine Item nach."
>
> Translation: "Online would naturally be easier: when you need a new item, it appears for us as 'please add it,' and we work through it per product or supplier and add that item."
>
> Code: #code/editable-structured-records, #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data

> "U. C. I. ist in dem Fall sehr gut, weil einfach alle Zugriff haben."
>
> Translation: "UCI is very good in this case because everyone has access."
>
> Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Wir haben fur die R. A. Mitarbeiter im Prinzip Adminrechte, also die sehen einfach alle Projekte und konnen uberall auch andern und eintragen und Messages schreiben."
>
> Translation: "Our Regulatory Affairs employees essentially have administrator rights: they see all projects and can change, enter, and write messages everywhere."
>
> Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "Also automatisierte Anpassungen wurde ich gerne ausschliessen. Wenn dann mit Frage."
>
> Translation: "I would like to exclude automated changes. If anything, they should happen with a question."
>
> Code: #code/automation-requires-user-confirmation

> "Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut."
>
> Translation: "The AI could say that a related item also needs changing and ask whether it should do that; I could actively choose yes or no, and that would be acceptable or even good."
>
> Code: #code/automation-requires-user-confirmation

> "Eventuell kann K. I. da auch in der Guidance helfen, ja, also gerade so gewisse Fragestellungen, die halt da aufpoppen zwecks Verlinkung oder Ahnliches."
>
> Translation: "AI could also help with guidance, especially for questions that arise about linking or similar matters."
>
> Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Man kann ja dieses diesen Vierseiter, dieses Application mit all ihren Kreuzchen und Eintragchen ja wunderbar digital abbilden und am Ende mit Submit drucken."
>
> Translation: "This four-page application with all its check boxes and entries could be represented digitally and submitted at the end."
>
> Code: #code/editable-structured-records

> "Wenn ich jetzt reingehen konnte in das Projekt und ich musste mir diesen Draft gar nicht herunterladen, sondern ich hatte eine View-Ansicht und konnte direkt daneben einen Kommentar reinschreiben."
>
> Translation: "If I could enter the project and did not have to download the draft, but instead had a viewing mode and could write a comment directly beside it."
>
> Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Eure Quotation ist unterschrieben und schreibgeschutzt. Ich muss mir die runterladen, dann druck ich mir die noch mal ins PDF, damit die nicht mehr schreibgeschutzt ist."
>
> Translation: "Your quotation is signed and write-protected. I have to download it and print it again as a PDF so that it is no longer write-protected."
>
> Code: #code/pdf-signature-forces-print-scan

> "Das klappt eigentlich schon sehr gut, weil wir uns absprechen in dem monatlichen Call."
>
> Translation: "That actually works quite well because we coordinate in the monthly call."
>
> Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Wir wurden dann wahrscheinlich jemanden benennen, der da drauf achtet und die Aufgaben dann halt verteilt."
>
> Translation: "We would probably designate someone to monitor it and distribute the tasks."
>
> Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

Wenn wir das itembasiert oder produktbasiert updaten konnten, das ware, glaube ich, schon mal unheimlich hilfreich.
Diese ganzen Daten stehen bei uns mal unabhangig von S. A. P. Sie stehen ja naturlich irgendwo in der technischen Akte, aber sagen wir mal in 3, 4, 5 verschiedenen Dokumenten.
Wir mussen das ja erst mal bei euch anmelden und durfen ja auch nicht implementieren, bevor das approved ist.
Dann haben wir auch die Problematik, jetzt haben wir acht Tandems, acht Produktgruppen, die haben nicht immer was.

Wenn Sie einen neuen Supplier zum Beispiel eintragen, machen Sie die ganze neue Zeile gelb oder wenn Sie in irgendeiner Zelle was andern, machen Sie die Zelle gelb und schreiben mir vorne in der History auch recht ausfuhrlich gerne immer hin, was haben Sie denn gemacht und warum.

Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches.

Wenn ich jetzt bei einem den Eintrag eher fuge einen E. R. C. Code fur diese Seite hinzu und wenn da jetzt ein Icon ware, Information, Achtung, ERC Codes, blablabla, einfach so ein bisschen und ein paar Links, ja klar, ware naturlich immer toll.
Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer.

Online naturlich einfacher ware, ihr wollt ein neues Item haben und dann ploppt bei uns auf 'Bitte nachpflegen' und dann scrollen wir uns einfach durch pro Produkt oder pro Supplier und pflegen dieses eine Item nach.
U. C. I. ist in dem Fall sehr gut, weil einfach alle Zugriff haben.
Wir haben fur die R. A. Mitarbeiter im Prinzip Adminrechte, also die sehen einfach alle Projekte und konnen uberall auch andern und eintragen und Messages schreiben.
Also automatisierte Anpassungen wurde ich gerne ausschliessen. Wenn dann mit Frage.

Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut.
Eventuell kann K. I. da auch in der Guidance helfen, ja, also gerade so gewisse Fragestellungen, die halt da aufpoppen zwecks Verlinkung oder Ahnliches.
Man kann ja dieses diesen Vierseiter, dieses Application mit all ihren Kreuzchen und Eintragchen ja wunderbar digital abbilden und am Ende mit Submit drucken.
Wenn ich jetzt reingehen konnte in das Projekt und ich musste mir diesen Draft gar nicht herunterladen, sondern ich hatte eine View-Ansicht und konnte direkt daneben einen Kommentar reinschreiben.
Eure Quotation ist unterschrieben und schreibgeschutzt. Ich muss mir die runterladen, dann druck ich mir die noch mal ins PDF, damit die nicht mehr schreibgeschutzt ist.
Das klappt eigentlich schon sehr gut, weil wir uns absprechen in dem monatlichen Call.
Wir wurden dann wahrscheinlich jemanden benennen, der da drauf achtet und die Aufgaben dann halt verteilt.

notes.body:
# Interview P12: Regulatory strategy lead managing TUV submissions across a large trauma portfolio

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- The participant is the central point of contact for TUV for a large trauma portfolio at a J&J company.
- The participant manages changes, submissions, and certification-body communication end to end, except for onsite audits led by quality teams.
- The portfolio is large and varied. Appendix ABC contains about 36,000 stock keeping units across several classifications and custom-device cases.
- The participant wants predictable submissions, less duplicate Appendix ABC work, clearer role routing, and less repeated supplier-document handling.
- The participant values UCI, weekly contact with TUV contacts, and the application form, but reports that large-scale change handling still depends on manual tracking and spreadsheet work.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Anything basically that goes into TUV from the company goes through me. That's how we manage it, a central point of contact."
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Our portfolio is very large. So we have I think our appendixes are big. There are about 36,000 skews on them."
Code: #code/high-volume-product-data

> "So I meet with [our project handlers] like once a week."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "The application form is very straightforward. The only thing is copy and pasting, as I said, doesn't work very well, but. The new one that you've done, it was last year or something, it's much better."
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "We're never sure the level of detail that goes in. Is it purely so you guys can assess is it a change or not? So it's pretty high level. Or can we put in more to leverage previously reviewed items as well?"
Code: #code/application-detail-level-unclear

> "Sometimes it is confusing if it's QMS or if it's product, where it's, so for a high class change, if it's a design change, I always put in a product change. And then sometimes I get a feedback saying, oh, does GMS change as well?"
Code: #code/qms-product-change-routing-unclear

> "Because the appendix updates take so long, I just give [our project handler] an update that I'm updating the appendix for change. It's coming in a few weeks because it just takes me so long to update them."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "We just use Excel. We tried something more fancy, but it just wasn't worth it. So we find Excel works."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "I do find UCI. I download that once a week just to double check that I'm not missing anything. It works pretty well for that. That's why I really dislike a UCI if projects aren't categorized correctly, because it takes me forever then to cross reference them."
Code: #code/uci-project-categorization-needed

> "We've a lot of templates. So like for the application form, I have a pre-filled out template for adding a new supplier, for instance, because we do that so often."
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "There's no way for me to filter the appendix for those exact SKU numbers. So I have to go through them one at a time to reference the change on the appendix."
Code: #code/high-volume-affected-sku-identification

> "If I have more than 100, I can only do about 100 SKUs an hour doing that. So that's extremely slow for a large change."
Code: #code/high-volume-affected-sku-identification

> "When we're adding a new supplier, I have to update multiple appendixes. That just is very slow."
Code: #code/multi-appendix-supplier-update

> "The master contains both the old one and the future state, which is a bit confusing for everybody involved."
Code: #code/current-future-state-appendix-conflict

> "We got a deficiency last week from Rev 55. So like they're not using the new or even close to new version."
Code: #code/stale-appendix-review-reference

> "It takes away loads of the back and forth we used to have at the application stage asking us questions about stuff."
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "I do think changes should be its own column."
Code: #code/dedicated-change-reference-field

> "I don't think I should ever edit the master appendix personally. I think it should be managed by you and all I should ever do is application forms."
Code: #code/read-only-customer-master-data

> "The other thing, and it's a small thing, you can't clear filters. You've got it turned off on the lot spreadsheet."
Code: #code/spreadsheet-scale-limitations

> "It doesn't really work past 2000 lines, the formatting. So sorry, 10,000 lines. I can't remember. So it's not really suitable for the amount of SKUs I have."
Code: #code/spreadsheet-scale-limitations

> "What they do have is a questionnaire on it, which we do quite like."
Code: #code/guided-service-specific-submission-requirements

> "So what we want, so for instance, if we're submitting, I don't know, a change on packaging or something like that, and you've already assessed the sterility, say, three times before."
Code: #code/application-detail-level-unclear; #code/supplier-document-rerequest-cost

> "And the questionnaire basically is like just a list of your full text file. And it's like, has this changed? Yes. And you give the document number and you submit it."
Code: #code/guided-service-specific-submission-requirements

> "UCI, I mean, it's gotten very positive feedback. We really like it."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "It takes me two seconds to fill out. So it's fine. It's the other, it's the cross-linking the suppliers, the sterility locations, sterility type or that kind of one. That's the one that takes forever."
Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "But we can't update our UDI data until the change is approved."
Code: #code/regulatory-approval-gates-data-synchronization

> "They're just one final sum, which we don't love, but they still come individually and they're usually quite accurate."
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "What is very, very difficult because a lot of people submitting changes, as I say, work with BSI and TUV in our company is the timelines."
Code: #code/timeline-model-hard-to-explain

> "Simple change or full text file submission takes the same length of time. And that is such a difficult message to get across to people."
Code: #code/timeline-model-hard-to-explain

> "We never put in a goal date because we, again, sometimes we'll get no deficiencies, sometimes we'll get three, and because each deficiency round adds 8 weeks."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "So you're right, you're very consistent. I know exactly probably when we're going to get it, but it's consistently long is the problem."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Our suppliers are getting very frustrated with us requesting the same documents and we're not allowed to hold their documents in our QMS."
Code: #code/supplier-document-rerequest-cost

> "We've won sterility cycle that's been reviewed 27 times and every time it's had a deficiency even though it's fine."
Code: #code/supplier-document-rerequest-cost

> "If there was like a Dropbox for suppliers they could use, it would be great because a lot of these, sometimes we have issues where they don't want to share something with us because competitor information is part of it."
Code: #code/supplier-direct-document-upload

> "Basically, they don't really need to see our information. The Dropbox is really all they need. Just that they do it and that we could see that it was done without them to see what was done would be great."
Code: #code/supplier-direct-document-upload; #code/role-based-data-governance

> "I mean, we do like to see it sometimes just to make sure, because sometimes, honestly, what they send us isn't good enough. We have to send it back for rework and stuff."
Code: #code/supplier-direct-document-upload; #code/supplier-document-rerequest-cost

> "What I love about UCI is the history. I've got all my projects there open and closed."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "I'd like to be able to separate out my QMS and my product projects or say renewals versus surveillances and stuff like that."
Code: #code/uci-project-categorization-needed

> "I have what 50 a year and I have to go into each one of those and add the PSUR team one at a time and that takes forever."
Code: #code/bulk-project-access-management

> "I'd like it easier for your reviewers to use as well so they don't be asking us loads of questions that we've already answered on the appendix."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "I'd like if it linked to the supplier certs so that I don't have to, so at the moment I upload all of our certs onto a SharePoint and [our project handler] shares them out."
Code: #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation

> "I don't put them in with every change application. We have too many."
Code: #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation

> "It would be nice if it linked to the supplier certs so that I don't have to, so at the moment I upload all of our certs onto a SharePoint and [our project handler] shares them out."
Code: #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation

> "I would like if there's a field for classification change or whatever you want to call it, designation change."
Code: #code/editable-structured-records

> "I personally would like if it linked to the PSUR and the SSCPs, that would make my job way easier."
Code: #code/portfolio-level-data-overview

> "As soon as the review is finished and it closes, it goes into a black hole of dates."
Code: #code/certification-body-status-black-box

> "I would love to be able to download every field on UCI basically."
Code: #code/project-data-export-needed

> "If we're paying expedited or dedicated, which is extremely expensive compared to your competitors, but it only works in the review portion, not the internal review and the certification board part."
Code: #code/timeline-model-hard-to-explain

> "I would like if when I'm loading my SKUs up, I can just take ISO, MEDSAP, MDR or whichever. So I don't have to do any duplication."
Code: #code/bulk-data-entry-needed

> "I would like the appendix to be a read only document for me."
Code: #code/read-only-customer-master-data

> "If we had your response is due in two days, I would love if that went to everyone who owned your project."
Code: #code/response-reminder-digest

> "I would like if we could separate technical questions from project management questions."
Code: #code/role-specific-notification-routing

> "UCI has cut down the amount of emails, I mean, humongously. So it's amazing."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "If there was just an overview page, it would be nice."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

## Theme Match

| Code(s) | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/high-volume-product-data; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/high-volume-affected-sku-identification; #code/multi-appendix-supplier-update; #code/spreadsheet-scale-limitations | [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]] | Direct confirmation. P12 describes high-volume SKU identification, supplier changes across several appendices, broken filters, disabled formulas, and spreadsheet scale limits. |
| #code/stale-appendix-review-reference; #code/current-future-state-appendix-conflict | [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]] | Direct confirmation. P12 reports that reviewers work from old Appendix ABC revisions while the customer has already moved to later revisions. |
| #code/uci-project-categorization-needed; #code/personal-excel-process-tracking; #code/unclear-process-timing; #code/certification-body-status-black-box | [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] | Direct confirmation. P12 needs categorized projects, overview, and visibility after review closure. |
| #code/response-reminder-digest; #code/role-specific-notification-routing; #code/bulk-project-access-management | [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]] | 2026-08-11: repointed from the split visibility mega-theme; these codes describe reminders, notification routing, and per-project access setup. bulk-project-access-management remains single-interview standalone pain-point evidence, not a confirmed theme code. |
| #code/project-data-export-needed | [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]] | 2026-08-11: repointed; this code is tracked as related evidence on the portfolio-visibility theme, not the split visibility mega-theme. |
| #code/eudamed-data-reuse; #code/bulk-data-entry-needed; #code/editable-structured-records | [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] | Direct confirmation: P12 wants EUDAMED reuse, bulk SKU loading, and directly editable structured records instead of duplicate entry. |
| #code/regulatory-approval-gates-data-synchronization; #code/read-only-customer-master-data | [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] | Direct confirmation: P12 wants approval-gated synchronization and read-only customer access to master data. |
| #code/portfolio-level-data-overview | [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]] | Direct confirmation: P12 wants certificate data linked to PSURs and SSCPs in one consolidated view. |
| #code/supplier-direct-document-upload; #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation | Standalone preliminary finding | Single-interview evidence describing a different actor (supplier, not customer) and a different data type (documents, not structured records). Not merged into any theme; needs cross-interview validation before promotion to a theme or need. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works; #code/shared-certification-repository; #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow | [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]] | Direct confirmation. P12 values weekly TUV contact, UCI history, and the application form as working supports. |
| #code/opaque-review-costs; #code/timeline-model-hard-to-explain | [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]] | Direct confirmation. P12 says quotations arrive as one final sum and that fixed timeline models are difficult to explain for simple changes. |
| #code/application-detail-level-unclear; #code/qms-product-change-routing-unclear; #code/dedicated-change-reference-field; #code/supplier-document-rerequest-cost | No exact existing theme | These remain pain-point or related-evidence candidates. These mechanisms are concrete, but do not by themselves justify a new theme from P12 alone. |

## Positive / Working Patterns Checked
- P12 directly confirms that weekly named TUV contact and project-handler contact work well.
- P12 directly confirms that UCI history and project access reduce email dependency and support vacation coverage.
- P12 directly confirms that the application form is easy to use and improved over the previous version.
- These observations match existing positive patterns where applicable. No new positive-pattern note is created from one interview alone.

## Research Gaps / Validation Questions
- Validate whether application forms should capture planned submission evidence and previously reviewed evidence references.
- Validate whether product and quality-management-system change routing requires clearer service guidance.
- Validate whether supplier direct upload can satisfy regulatory evidence ownership while protecting supplier-sensitive content, limiting supplier visibility, and allowing the manufacturer to track completion.
- Validate whether read-only customer access to master certification data reduces edit risk without slowing change submissions.

| Supplier certificates and linkages | Supplier certificates are uploaded to SharePoint and shared manually; supplier, sterility location, and sterility type cross-linking takes effort; `#code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation`; `#code/fragmented-product-data-sources`; `#code/portfolio-level-data-overview` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need a consolidated view of products, suppliers, sites, and shared data]]; [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] | None |
| UDI and approval-gated synchronization | UDI data is easy, but source changes cannot be updated before approval; `#code/eudamed-data-reuse`; `#code/regulatory-approval-gates-data-synchronization`; `#code/read-only-customer-master-data` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need to reuse European Database on Medical Devices (EUDAMED) product data]]; [[Customers need to approve consequential certification-data updates before application]]; [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]] | Validate whether read-only master access slows change submissions. |

| Access and notifications | Bulk project access, response reminders, and role-specific routing are needed; `#code/bulk-project-access-management`; `#code/response-reminder-digest`; `#code/role-specific-notification-routing` | Captured mechanism | [[Bulk project teams must be added one project at a time]]; [[Customers need dependable alerts when deficiency questions require a response]]; [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] | Bulk project access remains preliminary until confirmed elsewhere. |
| UCI history and named TUV contact | Weekly contact, UCI history, email reduction, and improved application form work well; `#code/auditor-guidance-works`; `#code/shared-certification-repository`; `#code/guided-end-to-end-workflow` | Positive pattern | [[Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information]]; [[UCI keeps active project requests, messages, and documents together]] | None |
| Dedicated change reference | Customer wants a separate change column because comments can be lost; `#code/dedicated-change-reference-field` | Captured mechanism | [[Customers need their change-notification ID retained through the TUV process]] | None |

notes.body:
# Theme: Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages

## Definition
Customers understand the main certification stages, but cannot reliably see current timing, task ownership, or status once work moves between stages or to the certification body. They keep personal trackers and want to find and follow a project's status in one place.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 after a discriminant-validity review found this theme bundled at least five distinct mechanisms (22 codes, 13 linked pain points) under one "visibility" title: status/timing opacity, notification configuration, platform/channel fragmentation, request-initiation and signature friction, and bulk access provisioning. This theme keeps only the codes describing status, timing, ownership, and findability of a project's current state. See Related themes below for the successor themes.

## Associated codes
- #code/unclear-process-timing
- #code/personal-excel-process-tracking
- #code/request-progress-visibility
- #code/certification-body-status-black-box
- #code/task-ownership-not-visible
- #code/customer-change-id-not-retained
- #code/project-search-by-customer-identifier
- #code/uci-project-categorization-needed

## Representative quotes
> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear." - P01

> "Personally, I maintain tracking of the approaches in an Excel file, signing the steps of the file." - P01

> "Was man nicht hat, ist den Request Progress. Der finde ich sehr transparent noch." - P02
>
> Translation: "What one does not have is the request progress. I find that very transparent."

> "Changes, assessment status, also deficiency status... timelines regarding the status, the expected closure date." - P03

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."

> "Die sehe ich nie wieder, weder auf der Rechnung noch auf der Rückmeldung." - P04
>
> Translation: "I never see it again, neither on the invoice nor on the feedback."

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten." - P06
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?" - P07
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"

> "Das hab ich auch schon mal angemerkt, dass man da nicht sehen kann, wann der Service Request wirklich übermittelt wurde. Ich glaub, da steht nur 'zuletzt bearbeitet' Stand oder sowas wird angezeigt." - P09
>
> Translation: "I have already pointed out that you cannot see when the service request was actually submitted. I think it only shows a 'last edited' status or something similar."

> "Und wenn wir da 'ne Möglichkeit hätten, über den Produktname oder noch besser tatsächlich über die Technical File Nummer bei uns, den R.M.F. Wenn wir das finden würden, das wäre natürlich super, weil wir so immer überlegen, was ja, haben wir da schon 'n Projekt gehabt, zu welchem Zeitpunkt kommt das ASA Projekt, wann erwarten wir das, also da ist die die Suche danach immer relativ schwierig." - P09
>
> Translation: "If we could find it by product name or, even better, by our technical-file number, the RMF, that would be excellent because we currently have to work out whether we already had a project, when the ASA project is coming, and when to expect it; finding it is relatively difficult."

> "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. fürs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prüfung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prüfung, das ist O.K. Ich wüsste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen könnte in der Übersicht. Das wäre ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TÜV. Das sieht man primär nicht." - P10
>
> Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; [the manufacturer] owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."

> "Aber sagen wir mal, die Zwischendinger die Zwischenmeilensteine, die sieht man jetzt aktuell nicht in der Übersicht, wo du sagst, okay, der TÜV antwortet bis dahin oder wir müssen dann bis 90 Tage danach oder was auch immer dann ein Feedback geben, dass man sowas auch in der Übersicht sieht." - P10
>
> Translation: "The intermediate milestones are not currently visible in the overview, such as when TUV will respond or when we must give feedback within 90 days."

> "I really dislike a UCI if projects aren't categorized correctly, because it takes me forever then to cross reference them." - P12

> "As soon as the review is finished and it closes, it goes into a black hole of dates." - P12

> "If there was just an overview page, it would be nice." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
Genuine tension within this construct: every participant confirms the main certification phases are named and known, but the degree of loss narrows or widens by stage. P01, P02, P03, and P06 report that status stays visible while a request is active in UCI. P04, P05, P09, P10, and P12 report that visibility specifically breaks once work reaches the certification body, a deficiency review, or task handoff — the timing, current owner, and intermediate milestones become invisible even though the overall phase name is still shown.

## Open questions
Confidence remains High: P12 provides a tenth direct confirmation and adds project categorization, an overview page, and post-review status. Test which dates, owners, status transitions, and searchable identifiers would be actionable enough to replace personal tracking.

## Related themes
- [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]
- [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]

## Linked pain points
- [[Customers cannot see timing or current status between certification steps]]
- [[Customer change-notification IDs are lost across TUV correspondence and billing]]
- [[Submitted requests show edit history instead of submission time]]

## Linked insights
- [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]]

frontmatter.segments: Regulatory Affairs Manager; Quality Management System lead; Associate director for European regulatory strategy at a large medical-device manufacturer

notes.body:
# Theme: Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance

## Definition
Before accepting a quotation, customers cannot always see the cost breakdown or why an assessment module is included. This makes it hard to plan a budget or question the proposed scope.

## Associated codes
- #code/opaque-review-costs
- #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale
- #code/timeline-model-hard-to-explain

## Representative quotes
> "Und dort wissen wir ganz genau, was ein Experte kostet und wie viel nachher der Experte für einen Review abgerechnet hat." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we know exactly what an expert costs and how much the expert charged for a review."

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?" - P07
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

> "They're just one final sum, which we don't love, but they still come individually and they're usually quite accurate." - P12

> "Simple change or full text file submission takes the same length of time. And that is such a difficult message to get across to people." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
P02 understands which certification service to request; the uncertainty concerns cost and assessment-module scope, not basic service selection. P07 also needs routine-cost estimates but reports that explanations arrive only after repeated follow-up.

## Related evidence
P09 reports that additional technical-documentation requests can emerge during assessment and that change types require repeated clarification about documents and modules. This is adjacent to scope predictability, but it does not directly confirm missing pre-quotation cost or module rationale, so interview and quote counts are unchanged.

## Open questions
Confidence increases to High: P12 provides a third direct confirmation and adds fixed timeline-model explanation as a commercial planning problem. Test which explanation, cost breakdown, timeline model, and forecast would be sufficient for customers to predict and challenge scope before quotation acceptance.

## Linked pain points
- [[Customers cannot predict quotation costs or included assessment modules]]

## Linked insights
No insight yet: two interviews directly support this theme, but it has not connected strongly enough to a second theme to justify an insight.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Theme: Customers need bulk product data entry, reuse across certificates, and portfolio visibility (superseded)

## Superseded note
This theme bundled 19 codes and 35 quotes spanning at least four distinct mechanisms, which is a discriminant-validity failure: a high code count under one theme, quotes clustering into unrelated topic areas, and a "Contradicting evidence" section that read as a per-participant list rather than a genuine tension within one construct. On 2026-08-11 it was split into four narrower themes, each with its own definition, associated codes, and representative quotes:

- [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] — data-entry effort and reuse (`bulk-data-entry-needed`, `eudamed-data-reuse`, `reuse-issued-supplier-certificates`, `editable-structured-records`, `guided-end-to-end-workflow`, `development-data-evolves`)
- [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] — integration-channel maturity spectrum (`system-to-system-data-integration`, `automated-data-validity-checks`, `bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity`)
- [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] — governance, approval, and traceability (`role-based-data-governance`, `shared-data-audit-trail`, `change-reminder-for-distributed-data`, `read-only-customer-master-data`, `exemplar-submission-disconnected-from-change-scope`, `automation-requires-user-confirmation`, `regulatory-approval-gates-data-synchronization`)
- [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]] — portfolio-level overview and reporting (`portfolio-level-data-overview`, plus related-evidence-only codes `certification-process-performance-metrics` and `project-data-export-needed`)

Two codes evidenced only in P12 (`supplier-direct-document-upload`, `supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation`) describe a distinct actor (supplier, not customer) and a distinct data type (documents, not structured records). Per the vault's two-interview theme-confirmation rule, these were not folded into any of the four themes above or promoted to a theme of their own. They remain a standalone, single-interview observation, flagged in [[P12]]'s Theme Match table and awaiting cross-interview validation.

A data-integrity issue was also found during the split: P05 was counted in this theme's `interview_count`/`quote_count` and had two quotes listed above, but [[P05]]'s own Theme Match table never linked P05's codes to this theme as a direct confirmation. P05 is not carried into any of the four successor themes.

All downstream references (interview Theme Match tables, needs, insights, personas, topic coverage register) have been repointed to the four successor themes above. This note is kept for traceability and should not be deleted or reused for new content.

# Theme: Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate

## Definition
Participants want to provide product, supplier, and certificate data once, in bulk or through guided entry, and have it reused across certificates and change requests, instead of retyping the same values reference by reference for every scheme, template, or submission.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 from the former theme [[Customers need bulk product data entry, reuse across certificates, and portfolio visibility]] after a discriminant-validity review found that theme bundled at least four distinct mechanisms under one title. This theme keeps the codes describing data-entry effort and reuse only; integration-channel preference, governance/approval, and portfolio-level visibility now live in separate themes (see Related themes below).

## Associated codes
- #code/bulk-data-entry-needed
- #code/eudamed-data-reuse
- #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates
- #code/editable-structured-records
- #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow
- #code/development-data-evolves

## Representative quotes
> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information." - P01

> "Ich kann sie natürlich defenden, weil sie teilweise einfach nicht da ist zu einem Entwicklungsprojekt." - P02
>
> Translation: "Of course, I can defend this because it is sometimes simply not available yet for a development project."

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information." - P03

> "Wenn mein Supplier 'n TÜV-Süd Zertifikat habt, dass ihr euch das selber zieht. Ihr habt es schließlich auch ausgestellt." - P04
>
> Translation: "When my supplier has a TUV SUD certificate, you should retrieve it yourselves. After all, you issued it."

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden." - P06
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"

> "Das ist natürlich auch unser Wunsch, dass man 'ne Situation hat, wo man bei uns in der in der Datenbank 'ne Information einträgt und der Datensatz, wenn er dann komplett ist, halt auch transferiert werden kann, so wie das für die Eutermed auch funktioniert, dass man da nichts händisch eintragen muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "Our wish is to enter information in our database and transfer the record once it is complete, as with EUDAMED, so that nothing has to be entered manually."

> "Wie gesagt, so gut es geht digital zu haben, kein PDF mehr ausdrucken zu müssen, um irgendwas reinzugeben und dann ist digital zu unterschreiben, wie auch immer das da der Austausch da ist." - P10
>
> Translation: "As far as possible, it should be digital: no more printing PDFs to enter something and then signing digitally."

> "Wenn wir das itembasiert oder produktbasiert updaten konnten, das ware, glaube ich, schon mal unheimlich hilfreich." - P11
>
> Translation: "If we could update it by item or product, that would be extremely helpful."

> "I would like if when I'm loading my SKUs up, I can just take ISO, MEDSAP, MDR or whichever. So I don't have to do any duplication." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
No direct contradiction found; every interview describing this construct agrees on the core need to avoid duplicate entry. Participants differ only in preferred mechanism (guided step-by-step forms in P06 versus directly editable structured records in P10 and P11), which reflects a UI preference rather than disagreement about the underlying need.

## Data-integrity note
P05 was included in the former theme's interview and quote counts, but P05's own interview note ([[P05]]) does not record any code from this cluster as a direct confirmation of it. P05 is excluded from this theme's counts; its two quotes formerly cited here (about internal metadata systems and wanting more metrics) were not genuine evidence for this specific mechanism.

## Open questions
Confirm whether "guided workflow" and "directly editable records" are genuinely the same underlying need (reduced entry effort) or should themselves be split further once more interviews are available.

- [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]]

## Linked pain points
No current-state pain point is linked yet; this is a future-state requirement theme.

## Linked insights

frontmatter.name: Governance Approval and Audit Trail
frontmatter.segments: Regulatory Affairs Manager; Quality Management System Manager; Quality Management System lead; Cross-functional certification stakeholders; Cross-functional regulatory and quality team at a large medical-device manufacturer; Regulatory Affairs team at a medical-device manufacturer; Associate director for European regulatory strategy at a large medical-device manufacturer

notes.body:
# Theme: Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data

## Definition
Participants need scoped contributor and approver roles, a traceable change history, and explicit approval gates before shared certification data is created, changed, or synchronized, so that manufacturer data ownership and TUV review responsibilities stay distinct and traceable.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 from the former theme [[Customers need bulk product data entry, reuse across certificates, and portfolio visibility]] after a discriminant-validity review. This theme groups all codes about who may change shared data, how changes are approved, and how those changes are tracked, separating governance from data-entry mechanics and integration-channel preference.

## Associated codes
- #code/role-based-data-governance
- #code/shared-data-audit-trail
- #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data
- #code/read-only-customer-master-data
- #code/exemplar-submission-disconnected-from-change-scope
- #code/automation-requires-user-confirmation
- #code/regulatory-approval-gates-data-synchronization

## Representative quotes
> "Was ist, wenn sich was ändert? Ich denk, das ist das größte Thema von allem. Wie merk ich das? Denk ich auch daran, dass ich dort auch noch was ändern muss, weil das wird jetzt immer signifikant schlimmer." - P02
>
> Translation: "What happens when something changes? I think that is the biggest issue of all. How do I notice it? Do I also remember that I have to change something there, because it is becoming significantly worse now?"

> "I would prefer to have notification in order to be sure that there is a reminder, we are not missing anything." - P03

> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird, sollte es vielleicht auch eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die dann quasi die Approvals macht." - P07
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data is maintained, there should perhaps also be a higher-level role that handles the approvals."

> "Also ich würd es, glaub ich, nicht begrüßen, wenn sie eigenständig ändern." - P08
>
> Translation: "I don't think I would welcome it if they changed things independently."

> "Dann vielleicht auch mit dem Status 'ne klare Abgrenzung, was jetzt 'Covered by Certificate' ist." - P09
>
> Translation: "Then perhaps also a clear distinction in status for what is 'covered by certificate.'"

> "Wir müssen aber immer im Hinterkopf behalten, wir haben da noch 100 andere Artikel, die eigentlich auch von dieser Änderung betroffen wären." - P09
>
> Translation: "But we always have to keep in mind that there are another 100 items that would actually also be affected by this change."

> "Also nachvollziehbar über 'ne Änderungshistorie wäre wichtig." - P09
>
> Translation: "Being traceable through a change history would be important."

> "Also automatisierte Anpassungen wurde ich gerne ausschliessen. Wenn dann mit Frage." - P11
>
> Translation: "I would prefer to exclude automated adjustments. If they happen, then only with a confirmation prompt."

> "But we can't update our UDI data until the change is approved." - P12

> "I would like the appendix to be a read only document for me." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
No direct contradiction found; every interview describing this construct wants manufacturer-side control preserved (approval gates, confirmation prompts, or read-only master data), consistent in direction across interviews.

## Open questions
Confirm whether "read-only master data" (P12) and "approval before automated changes" (P11) describe the same governance need or two distinct controls, once more interviews are available.

## Related themes
- [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]

## Linked pain points
No current-state pain point is linked yet; this is a future-state requirement theme.

## Linked insights
- [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]]

frontmatter.name: Integration Channel Maturity Spectrum
frontmatter.segments: Regulatory Affairs Manager; Quality Management System Manager; Regulatory Affairs specialists; Regulatory Affairs leaders; Quality Management System lead; Cross-functional certification stakeholders; Cross-functional regulatory and quality team at a large medical-device manufacturer; Senior Quality Management leaders at a global medical-device manufacturer

notes.body:
# Theme: Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration

## Definition
Participants describe a range of acceptable technical channels for exchanging certification data with TUV SUD, from Excel or template upload through to a system-to-system (API or database) interface, and want automated validity checks applied on whichever channel is used. The preferred channel appears to track each customer's internal system maturity rather than reflecting one universal preference.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 from the former theme [[Customers need bulk product data entry, reuse across certificates, and portfolio visibility]] after a discriminant-validity review. The code `bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity` was moved into this theme rather than the reusable-data-entry theme, because both of its supporting quotes (P02, P03) are specifically about accepting Excel or template upload as an alternative to a full system-to-system interface, not about avoiding duplicate entry.

## Associated codes
- #code/system-to-system-data-integration
- #code/automated-data-validity-checks
- #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity

## Representative quotes
> "Für mich reicht eigentlich, wenn es so ist, theoretisch bei Udemed. Und von dem her, es muss keine Machine to Machine sein. Ich denke, mit Excel hochladen ist für uns vollkommen in Ordnung." - P02
>
> Translation: "For me, it is enough if it is theoretically like EUDAMED. It does not have to be machine-to-machine. I think uploading Excel is completely fine for us."

> "The solution of machine system that speak together will be the best solution." - P03

> "The solution that we can upload, for example, information like clinical supplier, we can upload our templates, could be a good compromise for me." - P03

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export." - P04
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."

> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion." - P04
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."

> "Ich fänd es besser, wenn es eben nicht übers U.C.I. Portal gehen würde, sondern über 'ne definierte Schnittstelle, dass eben, ich sag mal in Realtime, ab dem Zeitpunkt, wo ich auf den Knopf drück, jetzt bitte senden, dass dann die Daten übertragen werden." - P06
>
> Translation: "I would prefer it not to go through the UCI portal but through a defined interface, so that in real time, from the moment I press send, the data are transferred."

> "Aber da hatte ich bei den Produkten schon einiges ausgefüllt gehabt, wo dann der [unser TUV-Kontakt] gesagt hat, nee, wenn ich das so und so angebe, müssen Sie die und die Prüfung machen, weil es ja so nicht richtig ist." - P06
>
> Translation: "I had already completed quite a few product entries where [our TUV contact] said that if I specify it this way, you have to perform certain assessments because it is not correct that way."

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber auszutauschen." - P07
>
> Translation: "But there is of course no digital interface yet to exchange information about the products themselves."

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank die Werte." - P08
>
> Translation: "We cannot currently just say at the push of a button, pull the values from this or that database."

> "Dann kommt es ganz oft mit Hashtag Wert Ausrufezeichen, wenn was nicht stimmt." - P08
>
> Translation: "It often comes back with a hashtag-value exclamation mark when something is wrong."

> "Wenn jetzt die Schnittstelle ein Standardformat ist, das wäre natürlich sehr gut." - P10
>
> Translation: "If the interface used a standard format, that would of course be very good."

## Contradicting evidence
Genuine tension within this construct: P02 explicitly states that Excel upload is sufficient and a machine-to-machine interface is not necessary, while P03, P04, P07, P08, and P10 describe a system-to-system or API interface as the preferred end state, with template or Excel upload accepted only as an interim compromise. This split appears to correlate with each customer's internal system maturity rather than with a shared preference, consistent with modeling this as a spectrum (Excel to Template to API) rather than one uniform need.

## Open questions
Validate whether channel preference tracks internal system maturity as hypothesized, by capturing each participant's current internal tooling in future interviews.

## Related themes
- [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]

## Linked pain points
No current-state pain point is linked yet; this is a future-state requirement theme.

## Linked insights
- [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]]

Wenn jetzt die Schnittstelle ein Standardformat ist, das wäre natürlich sehr gut.

notes.body:
# Theme: Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels

## Definition
Customers want one platform that covers the full certification workflow and stores documents, decisions, and communication together, instead of moving between UCI, email, phone, Teams, and paper for the parts the platform does not yet cover.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 from the former theme [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] after a discriminant-validity review found that theme bundled at least five distinct mechanisms under one title. This theme keeps the codes describing platform coverage, channel switching, and repository consolidation only; status/timing visibility and notification configuration now live in separate themes (see Related themes below).

## Associated codes
- #code/partial-platform-coverage
- #code/request-follow-up-requires-email
- #code/multiple-channel-context-switching
- #code/shared-certification-repository
- #code/document-organization-by-service

## Representative quotes
> "In this moment it's not work for all the project or for the whole activity." - P01

> "Ich hab mich dran gewöhnt, dass es nur via U.C.I. ist. Man kann gut darauf nachher referenzieren, wenn der Request mal liegen bleibt, dann schreib ich ein Mail." - P02
>
> Translation: "I have become used to it only being via UCI. You can refer to it well afterwards; when the request is left pending, then I write an email."

> "Da wird persönlich individuell benannt. Ja, ja, keine Chance." - P02
>
> Translation: "It is named personally and individually. No chance [of a consistent grouping]."

> "Maybe a common repository could be beneficial in order to work all on the same version." - P03

> "Ein Portal, ein Zugang, also ein Endprodukt oder wie auch immer man es nennen will." - P04
>
> Translation: "One portal, one access point, an end product, or whatever one wants to call it."

> "Im Moment machen wir alles über das U.C.I. Portal." - P06
>
> Translation: "At the moment, we do everything through the UCI portal."

> "Also es läuft aktuell sehr viel parallel zwischen E-Mail und UCI Portal." - P07
>
> Translation: "Currently, a great deal runs in parallel between email and the UCI portal."

> "Mit U.C.I. hat sich schon einiges verbessert, weil man da tatsächlich ja elektronisch diese Anträge stellen kann, dann auch zu diesen Projekten dann immer alles an einer Stelle in der Kommunikation und auch von den Projektdokumenten her hat." - P08
>
> Translation: "UCI has already improved quite a lot because applications can be submitted electronically and the communication and project documents are then all in one place for those projects."

> "In U.C.I. haben mehrere Personen Zugriff, das ist wirklich schon um Welten besser geworden, finde ich." - P09
>
> Translation: "Several people have access in UCI, and I think that has become worlds better."

> "Also ich hätte es eher so vielleicht als Thema, warum wir es angesprochen haben, so als Medienwechsel oder sowas genannt. Ja, also digital Papier, Telefon besprechen, Teams, weiß ich nicht. Da sind halt sehr viele Brüche drin." - P10
>
> Translation: "I would describe it more as media changes: digital, paper, discussing by phone, Teams. There are many breaks in between."

> "U. C. I. ist in dem Fall sehr gut, weil einfach alle Zugriff haben." - P11
>
> Translation: "UCI is very good in this case because everyone has access."

> "UCI has cut down the amount of emails, I mean, humongously. So it's amazing." - P12

> "What I love about UCI is the history. I've got all my projects there open and closed." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
Genuine tension within this construct, framed by scope rather than disagreement: where UCI already covers a workflow, participants confirm it works well as a consolidated repository (P09, P11, P12). The pain is specifically the parts UCI does not yet cover — Appendix ABC, non-UCI-managed projects and locations, pending-request follow-up, and document naming — which force continued email, phone, Teams, and paper use (P01, P02, P06, P07, P08, P10).

## Open questions
Confidence is High: 11 of 12 interviews directly confirm the same underlying need. Test which remaining workflows (Appendix ABC maintenance, pending-request follow-up, cross-location project coverage) would need to move into the platform to remove the last channel switches.

## Related themes
- [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
- [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]

## Linked pain points
- [[Partial platform coverage forces continued email and spreadsheet tracking]]
- [[Pending requests require email follow-up outside UCI]]
- [[Ungrouped service documents make request history difficult to manage]]
- [[Submitted application documents are hidden after project creation]]
- [[Customers cannot create UCI requests before TUV creates a project]]
- [[Write-protected TUV forms require print-and-scan workarounds]]

## Linked insights
No insight yet: this theme has not connected strongly enough to a second theme to justify a new insight (see Definitions.md insight-creation threshold).

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Theme: Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data

## Definition
Participants want a consolidated, portfolio-level view of their certification data, linked documents, and export options, distinct from the mechanics of entering or exchanging individual records.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 from the former theme [[Customers need bulk product data entry, reuse across certificates, and portfolio visibility]] after a discriminant-validity review. Only `portfolio-level-data-overview` is directly confirmed across two interviews; the other two codes below are single-interview related evidence and do not raise this theme's confidence.

## Confidence basis
Multi-interview: two distinct interviews (P01, P12) directly confirm the core mechanism (wanting one consolidated view instead of a fragmented one). This is below the vault's 25%-of-sample threshold for High confidence, so confidence is set to Medium and the theme is flagged for further validation.

## Associated codes
- #code/portfolio-level-data-overview (direct confirmation, P01 and P12)
- #code/certification-process-performance-metrics (related evidence only, P05; excluded from this theme's counts — see data-integrity note)
- #code/project-data-export-needed (related evidence only, P12)

## Representative quotes
> "With this kind of system we cannot have an overview and a summary of all the list of our devices with our devices with a list of all the study barrier sterilization process or main supplier." - P01

> "In parallel way will be very useful to have also the system that if this information can put in a table or Excel file in order to see also the same view of appendix ABC of today." - P01

> "I personally would like if it linked to the PSUR and the SSCPs, that would make my job way easier." - P12

> "I would love to be able to download every field on UCI basically." - P12

## Data-integrity note
`certification-process-performance-metrics` (P05) was represented in the former theme's quote list, but P05's own interview note ([[P05]]) links that code to a different theme ([[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]) as related evidence only, not to this construct. It is listed here as an associated code for traceability but is not counted as confirming evidence and its quote is not repeated in this file.

## Open questions
This theme currently rests on two interviews; validate the same mechanism (wanting one consolidated portfolio view, not just entry or export mechanics) in additional interviews before treating it as a stable, high-confidence theme.

## Related themes
- [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]

## Linked pain points
No current-state pain point is linked yet; this is a future-state requirement theme.

## Linked insights
None yet; evidence is not yet sufficient to justify a new insight for this construct alone (see Definitions.md insight-creation threshold).
