frontmatter.segments: Regulatory and quality assurance lead; Regulatory Affairs specialists; Regulatory Affairs managers; Regulatory Affairs leaders; Quality Management System lead; Cross-functional certification stakeholders; Cross-functional regulatory and quality team at a large medical-device manufacturer; Senior Quality Management leaders at a global medical-device manufacturer; Regulatory Affairs team at a medical-device manufacturer; Associate director for European regulatory strategy at a large medical-device manufacturer

notes.body:
# Theme: Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work

## Definition
When Appendix ABC is frozen for review but the customer keeps working in a new version, later reviewer comments must be copied into the current version by hand.

## Associated codes
- #code/revision-realignment-after-review
- #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision
- #code/shared-data-audit-trail
- #code/current-future-state-appendix-conflict
- #code/stale-appendix-review-reference

## Representative quotes
> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file." - P01

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon." - P04
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."

> "Es ist natürlich bei, ich weiß nicht wie viel Datenpunkten, sehr, sehr, sehr mühsam, das dann manuell nachzupflegen." - P04
>
> Translation: "With I do not know how many data points, it is of course very, very, very laborious to manually carry that forward."

> "Then they would kind of maintain like the most up-to-date versions on their end. So that part's a bit confusing to me, I suppose." - P05

> "I think if there's a better system for keeping things maintained and avoiding unintentional changes that then cause some synchronization issues, that would be preferable too." - P05

> "We also have tech doc reviews going on where we're being asked to change the appendices from that. So we've got multiple sources asking for changes at the same time." - P05

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist." - P07
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."

> "Unter den Versionswechseln habe ich manchmal gelitten, ne. Also wenn man da noch 'ne Spalte eingeführt hat oder sowas und aufgefordert war, da noch was und doch noch was zu verändern oder oder sowas." - P08
>
> Translation: "I have sometimes suffered under version changes, for example when another column was introduced and we were asked to change one thing and then another."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

> "Und da haben wir auch häufig den Fall, wir haben intern und Sie haben Änderungen gemacht und sich dann hinzusetzen und das wieder alles in eine Datei zu bringen, das ist wirklich viel Arbeit und auch fehleranfällig, dass der Kunde dann schreibt: 'O.K., meine Änderungen sind jetzt irgendwie nicht mehr in der Tabelle drinne.'" - P09
>
> Translation: "We often have the case where we made changes internally and you also made changes, and sitting down to bring everything back into one file is a lot of work and error-prone, so a colleague then writes that their changes are somehow no longer in the table."

> "Also da haben wir eigentlich auch keine Aufwände dann, außer dass wir die Mitarbeiter dann für ein paar Tage sperren müssen, an den Listen zu arbeiten." - P09
>
> Translation: "We do not really have any effort then, except that we have to prevent employees from working on the lists for a few days."

> "Gefühlt immer. Also ich warte immer, bis ich den letzten kriege." - P10
>
> Translation: "It feels like it happens all the time. I always wait until I receive the latest version."

> "Wenn wir Änderungen machen, dann sagen wir: 'Führ das bitte zusammen und schick mir die dann.' Das dauert aber dann auch." - P10
>
> Translation: "When we make changes, we say: please consolidate it and then send it to me. But that also takes time."

> "Wir haben immer eine offene Draftversion, da wird fleissig eingetragen, was so kommt, bis der Tag kommt, wo so, jetzt mussen wir mal ein Update schicken." - P11
>
> Translation: "We always have an open draft version where changes are entered until the day comes when we must send an update."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

> "The master contains both the old one and the future state, which is a bit confusing for everybody involved." - P12

> "We got a deficiency last week from Rev 55. So like they're not using the new or even close to new version." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
P04 successfully maintains a formal sequence of submitted and working versions for parallel changes, showing that disciplined internal versioning can reduce branching. P08 reports that TUV-performed version migration was easier, but customer-performed migration was too costly. P09 also says the agreed freeze-and-migrate process works well, but it requires a temporary editing stop and does not prevent reconciliation when both sides change data. P10 also relies on TUV to consolidate changes and waits for the latest version. P11 uses an open draft plus manual highlighting and history to manage changes until a formal update. These workarounds reduce migration effort without removing concurrent-state risk.

## Related evidence
P02 reports that MDR and MDSAP Appendix structures are not aligned. This creates related version complexity, but it is distinct from reconciling active revisions and concurrent incoming changes.

## Open questions
Confidence remains High: P12 provides a tenth direct confirmation and adds current/future state conflict plus stale-review revision use. Test whether record-level history, a shared current state, and explicit change provenance eliminate the need for manual reconciliation.

## Linked pain points
- [[Concurrent reviewer files require manual feedback realignment]]

## Linked insights
- [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]]
- [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]]

> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."

> "Es ist natürlich bei, ich weiß nicht wie viel Datenpunkten, sehr, sehr, sehr mühsam, das dann manuell nachzupflegen." - P04
>
> Translation: "With I do not know how many data points, it is of course very, very, very laborious to manually carry that forward."

> "Then they would kind of maintain like the most up-to-date versions on their end. So that part's a bit confusing to me, I suppose." - P05

> "I think if there's a better system for keeping things maintained and avoiding unintentional changes that then cause some synchronization issues, that would be preferable too." - P05

> "We also have tech doc reviews going on where we're being asked to change the appendices from that. So we've got multiple sources asking for changes at the same time." - P05

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist." - P07
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."

> "Unter den Versionswechseln habe ich manchmal gelitten, ne. Also wenn man da noch 'ne Spalte eingeführt hat oder sowas und aufgefordert war, da noch was und doch noch was zu verändern oder oder sowas." - P08
>
> Translation: "I have sometimes suffered under version changes, for example when another column was introduced and we were asked to change one thing and then another."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

> "Und da haben wir auch häufig den Fall, wir haben intern und Sie haben Änderungen gemacht und sich dann hinzusetzen und das wieder alles in eine Datei zu bringen, das ist wirklich viel Arbeit und auch fehleranfällig, dass der Kunde dann schreibt: 'O.K., meine Änderungen sind jetzt irgendwie nicht mehr in der Tabelle drinne.'" - P09
>
> Translation: "We often have the case where we made changes internally and you also made changes, and sitting down to bring everything back into one file is a lot of work and error-prone, so a colleague then writes that their changes are somehow no longer in the table."

> "Also da haben wir eigentlich auch keine Aufwände dann, außer dass wir die Mitarbeiter dann für ein paar Tage sperren müssen, an den Listen zu arbeiten." - P09
>
> Translation: "We do not really have any effort then, except that we have to prevent employees from working on the lists for a few days."

> "Gefühlt immer. Also ich warte immer, bis ich den letzten kriege." - P10
>
> Translation: "It feels like it happens all the time. I always wait until I receive the latest version."

> "Wenn wir Änderungen machen, dann sagen wir: 'Führ das bitte zusammen und schick mir die dann.' Das dauert aber dann auch." - P10
>
> Translation: "When we make changes, we say: please consolidate it and then send it to me. But that also takes time."

> "Wir haben immer eine offene Draftversion, da wird fleissig eingetragen, was so kommt, bis der Tag kommt, wo so, jetzt mussen wir mal ein Update schicken." - P11
>
> Translation: "We always have an open draft version where changes are entered until the day comes when we must send an update."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

> "The master contains both the old one and the future state, which is a bit confusing for everybody involved." - P12

> "We got a deficiency last week from Rev 55. So like they're not using the new or even close to new version." - P12
sections.Contradicting evidence: P04 successfully maintains a formal sequence of submitted and working versions for parallel changes, showing that disciplined internal versioning can reduce branching. P08 reports that TUV-performed version migration was easier, but customer-performed migration was too costly. P09 also says the agreed freeze-and-migrate process works well, but it requires a temporary editing stop and does not prevent reconciliation when both sides change data. P10 also relies on TUV to consolidate changes and waits for the latest version. P11 uses an open draft plus manual highlighting and history to manage changes until a formal update. These workarounds reduce migration effort without removing concurrent-state risk.
sections.Related evidence: P02 reports that MDR and MDSAP Appendix structures are not aligned. This creates related version complexity, but it is distinct from reconciling active revisions and concurrent incoming changes.

notes.body:
# Theme: Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources

## Definition
Keeping Appendix ABC up to date means manually bringing together a large product portfolio from several internal sources. Excel does not support this repeated reuse and update work well.

## Associated codes
- #code/versioned-excel-master-data
- #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance
- #code/high-volume-product-data
- #code/fragmented-product-data-sources
- #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel
- #code/misaligned-appendix-structures
- #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions
- #code/cross-tab-data-navigation
- #code/restricted-row-editing
- #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation
- #code/high-volume-affected-sku-identification
- #code/multi-appendix-supplier-update
- #code/spreadsheet-scale-limitations

## Representative quotes
> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated." - P01

> "We find some trouble in copy and paste the data from one to another file, not always being possible to edit the Excel." - P01

> "Nicht mal Appendix ABC von MDSAP und MDAR sind angeglichen." - P02
>
> Translation: "Not even Appendix ABC for MDSAP and MDR are aligned."

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel, weil ich brauche es ja eh, die Revision 09 vom MDR Appendix, weil der MDSAP Appendix brauch ich parallel jedes Jahr, weil der hat noch die ganzen Ablaufdaten hinten drin." - P02
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel because I need revision 09 of the MDR Appendix anyway; I also need the MDSAP Appendix in parallel every year because it still contains all the expiry dates."

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "We have to fill in again all the information for all products." - P03

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch." - P04
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."

> "Das Hin und Hergeklicke, das stimmt." - P04
>
> Translation: "All the clicking back and forth, that is true."

> "So now we're having to go back through now and do a complete assessment of the 10,000 CFNs and ensure that you know everything is accurate." - P05

> "The one that comes to mind most prominently is probably Appendix C for the suppliers." - P05

> "Das ist beim TÜV Süd auch 'ne Excel-Liste, wo halt aus meiner Sicht 'ne Tabellenkalkulationssoftware verwendet wurde, um 'ne Datenbank aufzubauen. Ist aus meiner Richtung nicht gut geeignet." - P06
>
> Translation: "At TUV SUD it is also an Excel list where, from my perspective, a spreadsheet application is being used to build a database. From my perspective, it is not well suited."

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam." - P06
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen." - P07
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind." - P07
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio." - P08
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."

> "Komplex machen es erstmal die ganz vielen Arbeitsmappen, das ist schon mal komplex, die unterschiedlichsten Informationen, die quasi seitens der benannten Stelle aus unserer Sicht erforderlich sind." - P08
>
> Translation: "What makes it complex first of all are the many worksheets and the very different kinds of information that, from our perspective, the notified body requires."

> "Wenn dann sich mal was in der Produktfamilie zum Beispiel in A. 3 ändert, dann denkt man vielleicht nicht dran, nach vorne zu springen. Es ist menschlich." - P08
>
> Translation: "If something changes in the product family, for example in A.3, people may not think to jump back to the front. It is human."

> "Also zum einen ist es, es sind es die Funktionen in der Excel-Liste, die limitiert sind, wenn man an mehrere 1000 Artikelnummern kommt." - P09
>
> Translation: "The functions in the Excel list are limited when you reach several thousand article numbers."

> "Wenn sich ein Zertifikat ändert, muss der Datensatz viermal angepasst werden, wo wurde vielleicht in einer Liste nicht angepasst, wurde vergessen, dann haben wir 2 Wahrheiten, welches Zertifikat gilt jetzt, das hat auch schon zu vielen Fragen geführt." - P09
>
> Translation: "When a certificate changes, the record has to be adjusted four times; perhaps one list was not updated or was forgotten, and then we have two versions of the truth about which certificate applies, which has already led to many questions."

> "Das, das, das, das meiste ist, glaube ich, dass man alles wieder neu eintragen muss, ja, weil sich ja gefühlt alle drei Wochen die Version oder Revision." - P10
>
> Translation: "The main issue is that you have to enter everything again because it feels as though the version or revision changes every three weeks."

> "Man muss eigentlich jede Zeile, jede Spalte, jede Zelle angucken, was man da jetzt wirklich eintragen muss." - P10
>
> Translation: "You essentially have to look at every row, every column, and every cell to determine what must be entered."

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen." - P11
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

> "Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer." - P11
>
> Translation: "The main pain points at present are that we have to maintain three appendices, in whatever form."

> "There's no way for me to filter the appendix for those exact SKU numbers. So I have to go through them one at a time to reference the change on the appendix." - P12

> "When we're adding a new supplier, I have to update multiple appendixes. That just is very slow." - P12

> "It doesn't really work past 2000 lines, the formatting. So sorry, 10,000 lines. I can't remember. So it's not really suitable for the amount of SKUs I have." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
Participants agree the data itself is necessary; they disagree only on how large the manual, duplicated maintenance burden is. P03 and P04 describe Appendix ABC as a bounded, required artifact that stays manageable as a side task. P06, P07, P08, and P10 describe the same maintenance as a growing burden once the spreadsheet reaches scale, spans multiple certificate-specific files, or must be re-entered row-by-row after a revision. P09 and P11 show a middle position: an agreed TUV-managed migration reduces customer effort but does not remove duplicate maintenance across certificate-specific lists. The problem is the manual, duplicated maintenance burden, not the purpose of the data.

## Open questions
Confidence remains High: P12 provides a twelfth direct confirmation and specifies large affected-SKU selection, supplier updates across several appendices, and spreadsheet scale limits. Test which supplier certificate and site fields can be sourced or verified automatically and which authorized record edits require audit controls.

_2026-08-11: Contradicting Evidence rewritten from an 11-participant roster into one tension (bounded side-task vs. growing burden at scale), per the new discriminant-validity checklist rule that this section must state a genuine tension, not a per-participant list._

- [[Large changing device portfolios make Appendix ABC maintenance labor-intensive]]
- [[Fixed Appendix rows require separate reference lists]]

## Linked insights
- [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]]
- [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]]

Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio.
Komplex machen es erstmal die ganz vielen Arbeitsmappen, das ist schon mal komplex, die unterschiedlichsten Informationen, die quasi seitens der benannten Stelle aus unserer Sicht erforderlich sind.
Wenn dann sich mal was in der Produktfamilie zum Beispiel in A. 3 ändert, dann denkt man vielleicht nicht dran, nach vorne zu springen. Es ist menschlich.
Also zum einen ist es, es sind es die Funktionen in der Excel-Liste, die limitiert sind, wenn man an mehrere 1000 Artikelnummern kommt.

Wenn sich ein Zertifikat ändert, muss der Datensatz viermal angepasst werden, wo wurde vielleicht in einer Liste nicht angepasst, wurde vergessen, dann haben wir 2 Wahrheiten, welches Zertifikat gilt jetzt, das hat auch schon zu vielen Fragen geführt.
Das, das, das, das meiste ist, glaube ich, dass man alles wieder neu eintragen muss, ja, weil sich ja gefühlt alle drei Wochen die Version oder Revision.
Man muss eigentlich jede Zeile, jede Spalte, jede Zelle angucken, was man da jetzt wirklich eintragen muss.

Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen.
Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer.
There's no way for me to filter the appendix for those exact SKU numbers. So I have to go through them one at a time to reference the change on the appendix.
When we're adding a new supplier, I have to update multiple appendixes. That just is very slow.
It doesn't really work past 2000 lines, the formatting. So sorry, 10,000 lines. I can't remember. So it's not really suitable for the amount of SKUs I have.

# Theme: Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information

## Definition
Named, responsive auditors help participants understand which information and documents they need before and during certification work.

## Associated codes
- #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Representative quotes
> "With [our auditor], we are quite well informed about the information needed." - P01

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity." - P01

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen." - P02
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "We have a weekly meeting with our project handler and coordinator." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung." - P06
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut." - P07
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."

> "Ich finde, wir sind eigentlich schon ziemlich gut in der Kommunikation, jetzt insbesondere durch U.C.I. die [unser TUV-Kontakt] als zentrale Ansprechpartnerin, also da dauert es keinen halben Tag, hat man 'ne Antwort oder zumindest, ich hab's weitergegeben, ich kümmere mich drum." - P09
>
> Translation: "I think communication is already quite good, especially through UCI and [our TUV contact] as the central contact; it takes less than half a day to receive an answer or at least confirmation that it has been forwarded and will be handled."

> "Das funktioniert aber eigentlich auch gut, da haben wir auch die Vereinbarung, wir sagten, wann die Listen quasi eingefroren sind, dann gehen die an den [unser TUV-Kontakt], der zieht die, migriert die mit einem Migration Tool oder irgendwas und dann kriegen wir sie wieder zur Verfügung gestellt und haben dann das neue Template verwendet mit den Daten aus der vorherigen Version." - P09
>
> Translation: "This actually works well: we agree when the lists are frozen, they go to [our TUV contact], he migrates them with a migration tool, and we receive the new template containing the data from the previous version."

> "Das sind ja so Situationen, wo wir mit [unserem TUV-Kontakt] dann sprechen. Wir arbeiten im [unserem TUV-Kontakt] ja schon, wie gesagt, seit keine Ahnung, also sind es 8 Jahre, 10 Jahre irgendwie so was zusammen. Und ich glaube auch, dass das wir gut mit ihm reden können und irgendwie eine Frage ist, dann hilft er uns jedes Mal und dann ist es halt auch für uns jetzt halt einfach, er ist ein vertrauter Kontakt, dem kann man was fragen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Those are situations where we speak with [our TUV contact]. We have worked with him for eight or ten years, can talk to him well, and whenever there is a question, he helps us; he is simply a trusted contact whom we can ask."

> "Das klappt eigentlich schon sehr gut, weil wir uns absprechen in dem monatlichen Call." - P11
>
> Translation: "That actually works quite well because we coordinate in the monthly call."

> "So I meet with [our project handlers] like once a week." - P12

> "UCI has cut down the amount of emails, I mean, humongously. So it's amazing." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
P01 also reports occasional unanswered requests for support, which may concern a different support channel or topic. P02, P03, P05, P06, P07, P09, P10, and P11 positive assessments depend on regular named contacts or recurring meetings and may not generalize to customers without this arrangement. P05 reports that system-only alerts can be missed, while P06 and P09 warn that over-notification can obscure relevant events.

## Open questions
Confidence remains High: P12 provides an eleventh direct confirmation that recurring human coordination and UCI project history reduce coordination effort. Test whether structured in-product guidance can preserve this tailored support without reducing access to a human contact.

## Linked pain points
None. This theme documents a working pattern.

## Linked insights
- [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]]

notes.body:
# Theme: Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones

## Definition
Certification-platform notifications are not scoped by urgency, access level, or task ownership. Depending on the participant's role, this either buries a critical alert among irrelevant ones or leaves a critical alert without a reliable channel, and a notification cannot be acknowledged as read without a separate action such as a download.

## Split note
Split on 2026-08-11 from the former theme [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]] after a discriminant-validity review found that theme bundled at least five distinct mechanisms under one title. This theme keeps the codes describing notification configuration, routing, and acknowledgement only; status/timing visibility and platform/channel consolidation now live in separate themes (see Related themes below).

## Associated codes
- #code/critical-uci-notification-missed
- #code/notification-subscriptions-not-separated-from-access
- #code/notification-read-state-requires-download
- #code/role-specific-notification-routing
- #code/response-reminder-digest

## Representative quotes
> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

> "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich überhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

> "Was mir jetzt so spontan einfallen würde, wenn 'ne Task geplant ist, dass jetzt zum Beispiel am 1.8. 'ne Bewertung für das Modul Sterilisation geplant ist, das vielleicht noch mal so 'n Reminder kommen könnte von U.C.I., bitte beachten. Am Montag startet die Bewertung, dass die Unterlagen bis dahin verfügbar sind." - P09
>
> Translation: "If a task is scheduled, for example an assessment of the sterilization module on August 1, UCI could send a reminder that the assessment starts on Monday and the documents must be available by then."

> "Dann sehe ich halt eine Notification. Die kann ich aber heute nicht gefühlt nicht als gelesen aktivieren. Die muss ich mir runterladen. Die will ich aber gar nicht runterladen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Then I see a notification. At present, I do not feel that I can mark it as read. I have to download it, although I do not want to download it."

> "If we had your response is due in two days, I would love if that went to everyone who owned your project." - P12

> "I would like if we could separate technical questions from project management questions." - P12

## Contradicting evidence
Genuine two-sided tension within the same construct: P06 and P09 report notification overload — irrelevant or high-volume alerts caused by access rights or subscriptions not matching a participant's actual responsibility. P05 and P12 report the opposite failure mode — a critical, action-required alert (a deficiency question, a response deadline) not reliably reaching the person who owns the task. Both failure modes trace back to the same root cause: notifications are not routed or scoped by role, urgency, or ownership.

## Open questions
Confidence is High: five distinct interviews (P05, P06, P09, P10, P12) directly confirm the same root mechanism. Test whether role-based routing, urgency-based digesting, and a lightweight one-click acknowledgement (without requiring a download) would resolve both the overload and the missed-alert failure modes.

## Related themes
- [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
- [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]

## Linked pain points
- [[Deficiency notifications without email alerts can remain unseen for weeks]]
- [[Coupled access and notification settings send administrators irrelevant alerts]]
- [[UCI notifications cannot be acknowledged without downloading files]]
- [[Bulk project teams must be added one project at a time]]

## Linked insights
- [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]]

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Pain Point Register

Last consolidated: 2026-07-30. All sixteen pain points were reviewed after P09. PP13 concerns action-required alerts that can be missed, while PP15 concerns subscriptions that cannot be scoped independently from access, so the underlying mechanisms remain distinct. PP14 concerns document continuity after project creation, while PP16 concerns the missing immutable timestamp before project creation.

P10 update: PP17 concerns customer-led request initiation before a project exists, PP18 concerns acknowledging an already-seen notification, and PP19 concerns completing a locked signed form. These mechanisms are distinct from PP07 request follow-up, PP13 missed action alerts, and existing document-continuity pains. P11 directly confirms PP01, PP02, and PP19; no new pain point is required because project-specific Appendix copying, open-draft reconciliation, and locked quotation rework match their existing underlying mechanisms. P12 directly confirms PP01, PP02, PP03, PP06, PP13, and PP15. PP20 concerns bulk project access assignment; PP21 concerns repeated supplier evidence requests. These are distinct from notification scoping and Appendix maintenance. A full consolidation is not due until three to five additional interviews after 2026-07-30.

2026-08-11 update: `Limited End-to-End Process Visibility` was split into three narrower themes after a discriminant-validity review (22 codes, 13 linked pain points bundled at least five distinct mechanisms). PP03, PP12, and PP16 stay under the renamed/narrowed `Certification Stage Timing and Ownership Opacity`. PP13, PP15, PP18, and PP20 move to the new `Undifferentiated Notification Routing`. PP05, PP07, PP08, PP14, PP17, and PP19 move to the new `Platform and Channel Consolidation`. No pain point's own evidence, severity, or confidence changed — only the Theme column was updated.

Central overview of all pain points. Updated by the agent after every interview (Step D3).
This is the working/sorting view — Themes and Insights remain the narrative layer for
stakeholders; this table is the evidence layer underneath.

Priority Tier = lookup from Severity × Confidence (see the "Priority Tier" matrix in
[[Definitions]], P0 = highest, P3 = lowest). Severity and Confidence are ordinal labels, not
numbers, so they are no longer multiplied together. Interview Count is a tie-breaker within a
tier, not a multiplier — when scanning rows that share a tier, check the higher Interview
Count first.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Bulk project teams must be added one project at a time

**Theme:** [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]
**Description:** Customers must add the same internal users to many related UCI projects one project at a time.
**Trigger:** A recurring project set, such as PSUR work, needs the same team access across many projects.
**Impact:** Access administration takes noticeable time and makes it harder to ensure that all responsible users can see the right projects.
**Workaround:** Add users manually to each project.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P12 describes the manual, one-at-a-time process directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P12

**Representative Quotes:**
> "I have what 50 a year and I have to go into each one of those and add the PSUR team one at a time and that takes forever." - P12

> "I would like if there was some sort of mass things like that, add the same people to the same project, stuff like that." - P12

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
Test bulk team assignment for recurring project groups, with confirmation before access changes are applied.

**Validation question:** Confirm whether other customers with recurring project sets must add the same users project by project.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Concurrent reviewer files require manual feedback realignment

**Theme:** [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]
**Description:** Reviewer comments, template changes, and customer working copies can create concurrent Appendix ABC states that require manual realignment into the active version.
**Trigger:** TUV SUD reviews or updates an Appendix while the customer continues work, or a revised template arrives alongside a customer revision.
**Impact:** Rework and risk of inconsistent data across customer and reviewer versions.
**Workaround:** Re-update the active revision after comments arrive and maintain an internal sequence of submitted and working versions.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 17
**Interview IDs:** P01, P04, P05, P06, P07, P08, P09, P10, P11, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file." - P01

> "Die Versionierung ist sehr, sehr schwierig." - P04
>
> Translation: "Versioning is very, very difficult."

> "Dann habe ich parallel eben die Arbeitsversion V24." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I have the working version V24 running in parallel."

> "Then they would kind of maintain like the most up-to-date versions on their end. So that part's a bit confusing to me, I suppose." - P05

> "We also have tech doc reviews going on where we're being asked to change the appendices from that. So we've got multiple sources asking for changes at the same time." - P05

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist." - P07
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

> "Und da haben wir auch häufig den Fall, wir haben intern und Sie haben Änderungen gemacht und sich dann hinzusetzen und das wieder alles in eine Datei zu bringen, das ist wirklich viel Arbeit und auch fehleranfällig, dass der Kunde dann schreibt: 'O.K., meine Änderungen sind jetzt irgendwie nicht mehr in der Tabelle drinne.'" - P09
>
> Translation: "We often have the case where we made changes internally and you also made changes, and sitting down to bring everything back into one file is a lot of work and error-prone, so a colleague then writes that their changes are somehow no longer in the table."

> "Gefühlt immer. Also ich warte immer, bis ich den letzten kriege." - P10
>
> Translation: "It feels like it happens all the time. I always wait until I receive the latest version."

> "Wenn wir Änderungen machen, dann sagen wir: 'Führ das bitte zusammen und schick mir die dann.' Das dauert aber dann auch." - P10
>
> Translation: "When we make changes, we say: please consolidate it and then send it to me. But that also takes time."

> "Wir haben immer eine offene Draftversion, da wird fleissig eingetragen, was so kommt, bis der Tag kommt, wo so, jetzt mussen wir mal ein Update schicken." - P11
>
> Translation: "We always have an open draft version where changes are entered until the day comes when we must send an update."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

> "The master contains both the old one and the future state, which is a bit confusing for everybody involved." - P12

> "We got a deficiency last week from Rev 55. So like they're not using the new or even close to new version." - P12

## Possible opportunity
Test shared revision states, review comments linked to a record, and explicit reconciliation flows.

frontmatter.name: Project Notification Subscriptions Cannot Be Scoped
frontmatter.theme: [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Coupled access and notification settings send administrators irrelevant alerts

**Theme:** [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]
**Description:** Project visibility and notification subscriptions are coupled, so administrators receive alerts for projects they need permission to see but do not personally manage.
**Trigger:** An administrator manages access across a shared company profile containing projects owned by multiple locations and colleagues.
**Impact:** High volumes of irrelevant notifications consume attention and make relevant project messages harder to identify.
**Workaround:** Manually inspect and dismiss notifications while retaining broad access rights.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview (P09 and P12 both directly describe the same coupling).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 4
**Interview IDs:** P09, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich überhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

> "Wenn ich da 'ne Möglichkeit hätte zu sagen, ich kann alle Projekte sehen, aber die Mitteilung zu den 5 Projekten, die möchte ich nicht haben, das zu deaktivieren, das wär super. Ich glaub, es geht technisch nicht." - P09
>
> Translation: "If I could say that I can see all projects but disable notifications for five of them, that would be excellent. I do not think that is technically possible."

> "I do say I've turned off the notifications off UCI because I have so many projects, there's too many." - P12

> "I would like if we could separate technical questions from project management questions." - P12

## Possible opportunity
Separate view and administration permissions from configurable notification subscriptions by project, owner, or customer-side responsibility.

# Pain Point: Customer change-notification IDs are lost across TUV correspondence and billing

**Theme:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
**Description:** The participant's change-notification ID is not retained in TUV correspondence, feedback, or invoices after the request receives a TUV project ID.
**Trigger:** Following a submitted change across TUV feedback, project communication, and billing.
**Impact:** The participant must repeatedly map project numbers back to internal change notifications, making parallel changes harder to trace.
**Workaround:** Maintain a separate list of open changes and manually look up the mapping.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P04 states the ID loss directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P04

**Representative quotes:**
> "Die sehe ich nie wieder, weder auf der Rechnung noch auf der Rückmeldung." - P04
>
> Translation: "I never see it again, neither on the invoice nor on the feedback."

## Possible opportunity
Test persistent display of a customer-provided change ID alongside the TUV project ID in all statuses, messages, documents, and invoices.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Customers cannot create UCI requests before TUV creates a project

**Theme:** [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]
**Severity/Confidence risk:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (see Definitions.md); this pain point's own mechanism is evidenced by only one interview (P10) even though it is linked to a multi-interview theme, so it should not be prioritized as if Confidence were High until a second interview directly confirms this specific mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P10 states this directly).
**Description:** Customers cannot create a request or significant-change record in UCI before TUV creates a project.
**Trigger:** A customer needs to start a new certification or significant-change request.
**Impact:** The first action depends on email or phone coordination and TUV setup rather than a customer-led, traceable workflow.
**Workaround:** Contact the project handler, exchange forms externally, and wait for a TUV-created project before uploading further material.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P10

**Representative quotes:**
> "UCI nutzen wir. Ja, ist okay. Allerdings muss man ja immer zuerst in U.C.I. muss ja ein Projekt eröffnet werden, bevor man dann irgendwas übermitteln kann, selbst wenn ich jetzt 'ne neue Anfrage hatte, 'ne Significant Change oder so, die kann ich, ich persönlich oder als Kunde kann ich im U.C.I. nicht draufklicken, mach mir was Neues auf und füll das dann da drin an." - P10
>
> Translation: "We use UCI. It is okay. However, a project must first be opened in UCI before you can submit anything; even when I have a new request or a significant change, I personally, as the customer, cannot click in UCI, create a new item, and complete it there."

## Possible opportunity
The workflow should provide customer-led request initiation with guided categorization, a submitted timestamp, and a linked handoff into the TUV project-creation workflow.

**Representative quotes:**
> "UCI nutzen wir. Ja, ist okay. >
> Translation: "We use UCI. It is okay. However, a project must first be opened in UCI before you can submit anything; even when I have a new request or a significant change, I personally, as the customer, cannot click in UCI, create a new item, and complete it there."

frontmatter.name: Opaque Cost and Assessment Scope
frontmatter.theme: [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]]

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Customers cannot predict quotation costs or included assessment modules

**Theme:** [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]]
**Description:** The customer cannot see a clear cost breakdown for reviews or reliably predict and contest assessment modules included in a quotation.
**Trigger:** Estimating a new certification, change, or annual routine cost before committing budget.
**Impact:** Cost estimates can change substantially, making budget planning unreliable and leaving the customer unable to influence assessment scope.
**Workaround:** Ask repeatedly for rationale and either accept the quoted scope or delay the work.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 6
**Interview IDs:** P02, P07, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "Und da haben wir auch keinen Durchblick in den Kosten, was da zusammenkommt." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we have no visibility into the costs that add up there."

> "Ich kann es dann akzeptieren oder nicht? Da habe ich als Hersteller gar keine Macht." - P02
>
> Translation: "I can then accept it or not? As a manufacturer, I have no power at all."

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?" - P07
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

> "They're just one final sum, which we don't love, but they still come individually and they're usually quite accurate." - P12

> "What is difficult is when people come to me and they do every week and they say, hey, we think we might need to put in the change, how much will it cost? And I'm like, oh my God, I have no idea." - P12

## Possible opportunity
Test an itemized pre-quotation breakdown that links each assessment module to the change rationale and shows the cost effect.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Customers cannot see timing or current status between certification steps

**Theme:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
**Description:** The participant understands the main certification phases but cannot reliably see timing or current status between steps.
**Trigger:** Managing an active certification request across departments and project types.
**Impact:** Uncertainty about progress, expected certificate timing, and whether TUV has received or reviewed a submission.
**Workaround:** Personally track project steps in Excel and ask the auditor.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 14
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P04, P05, P06, P07, P09, P10, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear." - P01

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie?" - P02
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, and when do they begin?"

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten." - P06
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

> "Wir haben zum Beispiel dieses Jahr im Audit erlebt, dass die Auditoren in einer Version vom Appendix A. B. C. nachgeschaut haben, die total outdated war." - P07
>
> Translation: "This year during the audit, the auditors reviewed a version of Appendix ABC that was completely outdated."

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?" - P07
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"

> "Was für uns aber das zentrale Datum ist es nicht, wann wir 'ne Rechnung erhalten, sondern wann wir das Approval kriegen." - P09
>
> Translation: "For us, the central date is not when we receive an invoice, but when we receive approval."

> "Da hat man jetzt, wir haben ja 'ne C.D. fürs Assessment eingereicht, das ist jetzt Projekt, das ist aktuell in Prüfung. Da gab's die die erste Deficiency als Frage. Da ist jetzt aber das Projekt hat den Status in Prüfung, das ist O.K. Ich wüsste jetzt nicht, wo man auf die Schnelle erkennen könnte in der Übersicht. Das wäre ein guter Punkt zu sagen, okay, wer hat denn gerade den Task? Denn aktuell hat Donnie den Task und nicht der TÜV. Das sieht man primär nicht." - P10
>
> Translation: "We submitted technical documentation for assessment and received the first deficiency question. The project status is 'under review,' but I would not know where to see at a glance who currently owns the task; [the manufacturer] owns it now, not TUV, and that is not primarily visible."

> "Aber sagen wir mal, die Zwischendinger die Zwischenmeilensteine, die sieht man jetzt aktuell nicht in der Übersicht, wo du sagst, okay, der TÜV antwortet bis dahin oder wir müssen dann bis 90 Tage danach oder was auch immer dann ein Feedback geben, dass man sowas auch in der Übersicht sieht." - P10
>
> Translation: "The intermediate milestones are not currently visible in the overview, such as when TUV will respond or when we must give feedback within 90 days."

> "We never put in a goal date because we, again, sometimes we'll get no deficiencies, sometimes we'll get three, and because each deficiency round adds 8 weeks." - P12

> "As soon as the review is finished and it closes, it goes into a black hole of dates." - P12

> "If we're paying expedited or dedicated, which is extremely expensive compared to your competitors, but it only works in the review portion, not the internal review and the certification board part." - P12

## Possible opportunity
Validate which status changes and forecast dates would be useful and reliable enough to display.

frontmatter.name: Critical UCI Notifications Can Be Missed
frontmatter.theme: [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Deficiency notifications without email alerts can remain unseen for weeks

**Theme:** [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]
**Description:** Deficiency questions can arrive in UCI without a reliable accompanying personal email, and high notification volume can cause the system alert to be overlooked.
**Trigger:** A reviewer issues a deficiency or question through UCI.
**Impact:** The manufacturer can discover action-required questions one to two weeks late, delaying its response and the review.
**Workaround:** Wait for personal email and periodically check UCI manually.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview (P05 and P12 both directly report missed or delayed notifications).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 3
**Interview IDs:** P05, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "There's been instances where like we've received deficiencies, but we're kind of old school, I guess, and so we wait for the e-mail." - P05

> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

> "Yeah, and I've missed one or two things myself, so 'cause if I miss putting them into my tracker, I have missed them." - P12

## Possible opportunity
Test a configurable, high-salience alert for action-required deficiencies, with clear acknowledgement and escalation states rather than increasing general notification volume.

## Related evidence
P09 reports receiving about 20 irrelevant notifications per week because administrator access automatically brings broad notification coverage. This supports the risk that high volume can hide important alerts, but P09 does not report a missed action-required message, so evidence and interview counts are unchanged.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Fixed Appendix rows require separate reference lists

**Theme:** [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]
**Description:** Fixed spreadsheet row permissions prevent the participant from inserting or deleting required product references in place, so the detailed reference list must be maintained in a separate synchronized attachment.
**Trigger:** A high-volume certificate needs a new, removed, or changed product reference.
**Impact:** Parallel reference lists increase manual synchronization work and make the complete product set harder to review.
**Workaround:** Maintain a separate reference-number appendix at the same version as Appendix ABC.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P04 states the fixed-row constraint directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P04

**Representative quotes:**
> "Wir haben aber die Ref-Nummern dann noch mal in einem von uns selber erstellten Anhang, den wir dann immer parallel noch pflegen und mitschicken." - P04
>
> Translation: "We keep the reference numbers again in a separately created appendix, which we maintain in parallel and send along."

> "Die eingeschränkten Rechte, also dass ich nicht Zeilen hinzufügen kann oder löschen kann." - P04
>
> Translation: "The restricted permissions, meaning that I cannot add or delete rows."

## Possible opportunity
Test structured records that allow authorized additions, removals, and relationship updates without creating a parallel reference list.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Large changing device portfolios make Appendix ABC maintenance labor-intensive

**Theme:** [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]
**Description:** Keeping Appendix ABC current is labor-intensive for a large, dynamically changing device portfolio.
**Trigger:** New or changing devices and codes require updates to the Appendix ABC file.
**Impact:** Significant recurring manual effort to maintain certification data.
**Workaround:** Maintain the file in Excel and create successive revisions after freezes.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 23
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07, P08, P09, P10, P11, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated." - P01

> "It is very tough because we have some thousands of code and then the number of devices is very high." - P01

> "Das ist ein Riesenaufwand schon." - P02
>
> Translation: "That alone is a huge effort."

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel." - P02
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel."

> "The Appendix ABC is really difficult to be maintained." - P03

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch." - P04
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."

> "So now we're having to go back through now and do a complete assessment of the 10,000 CFNs and ensure that you know everything is accurate." - P05

> "The one that comes to mind most prominently is probably Appendix C for the suppliers." - P05

> "Wir haben halt auch immer so, sag ich mal, doppelt und dreifach Pflege, weil jemand muss es ja auch in die Health Canada Datenbank eintragen, dann müssen wir es noch mal in das Appendix A. B. C. eintragen und dann noch mal in unser System eintragen." - P06
>
> Translation: "We also always have double and triple maintenance, because someone has to enter it in the Health Canada database, then we have to enter it again in Appendix ABC, and then again in our system."

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam." - P06
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen." - P07
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind." - P07
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio." - P08
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."

> "Also zum einen ist es, es sind es die Funktionen in der Excel-Liste, die limitiert sind, wenn man an mehrere 1000 Artikelnummern kommt." - P09
>
> Translation: "The functions in the Excel list are limited when you reach several thousand article numbers."

> "Wenn sich ein Zertifikat ändert, muss der Datensatz viermal angepasst werden, wo wurde vielleicht in einer Liste nicht angepasst, wurde vergessen, dann haben wir 2 Wahrheiten, welches Zertifikat gilt jetzt, das hat auch schon zu vielen Fragen geführt." - P09
>
> Translation: "When a certificate changes, the record has to be adjusted four times; perhaps one list was not updated or was forgotten, and then we have two versions of the truth about which certificate applies, which has already led to many questions."

> "Das, das, das, das meiste ist, glaube ich, dass man alles wieder neu eintragen muss, ja, weil sich ja gefühlt alle drei Wochen die Version oder Revision." - P10
>
> Translation: "The main issue is that you have to enter everything again because it feels as though the version or revision changes every three weeks."

> "Man muss eigentlich jede Zeile, jede Spalte, jede Zelle angucken, was man da jetzt wirklich eintragen muss." - P10
>
> Translation: "You essentially have to look at every row, every column, and every cell to determine what must be entered."

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen." - P11
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

> "Die Pain Points sind vor allem aktuell, dass wir drei Appendizes pflegen mussen, in welcher Art auch immer." - P11
>
> Translation: "The main pain points at present are that we have to maintain three appendices, in whatever form."

> "There's no way for me to filter the appendix for those exact SKU numbers. So I have to go through them one at a time to reference the change on the appendix." - P12

> "When we're adding a new supplier, I have to update multiple appendixes. That just is very slow." - P12

> "It doesn't really work past 2000 lines, the formatting. So sorry, 10,000 lines. I can't remember. So it's not really suitable for the amount of SKUs I have." - P12

## Possible opportunity
Test bulk update and reuse mechanisms that preserve Appendix ABC's function as a technical-data summary.

notes.title: Long assessment intervals make submitted change documentation outdated

frontmatter.name: Change Assessment Lags Internal Change Progress
frontmatter.validation_question: Do other customers also report difficulty keeping change assessments synchronized with faster internal changes, and what information falls behind?

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Long assessment intervals make submitted change documentation outdated

**Status:** `Standalone preliminary finding`; not yet a cross-interview theme.
**Validation question:** Do other customers also report difficulty keeping change assessments synchronized with faster internal changes, and what information falls behind?
**Validation status:** Needs cross-interview validation before this finding is treated as a pattern.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P03 states the mismatch directly).
**Severity/Confidence risk:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (see Definitions.md); this finding should not be prioritized as if Confidence were High until cross-interview validation confirms it — `needs-validation-before-prioritization` would apply once a second interview is added.
**Description:** Internal work continues while a submitted change awaits notified-body approval, so later changes may no longer match the submitted documentation.
**Trigger:** A change assessment has a long interval between submission and approval.
**Impact:** Implementation may be postponed, documentation becomes stale, and the company may need to use expedited assessment.
**Workaround:** Plan changes earlier and use monthly meetings or an expedited process when timing becomes critical.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative quotes:**
> "Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on." - P03

> "We try to plan as much as possible all the changes, but sometimes it's not possible and we need to use the expedite process." - P03

## Possible opportunity
Test shared assessment states, expected approval dates, and a mechanism to flag related internal changes before the submitted package becomes outdated.

frontmatter.name: Incomplete Change Impact Assessment Causes Resubmission
frontmatter.validation_question: Do other customers also have to resubmit change assessments because the initial impact analysis is incomplete, and which fields are most often missed?

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Missing affected departments or assessments cause change resubmission

**Status:** `Standalone preliminary finding`; not yet a cross-interview theme.
**Validation question:** Do other customers also have to resubmit change assessments because the initial impact analysis is incomplete, and which fields are most often missed?
**Validation status:** Needs cross-interview validation before this finding is treated as a pattern.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P03 states the omission directly).
**Severity/Confidence risk:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (see Definitions.md); this finding should not be prioritized as if Confidence were High until cross-interview validation confirms it — `needs-validation-before-prioritization` would apply once a second interview is added.
**Description:** Change coordinators can omit affected departments or assessments, and the gap is found only after submission or during implementation planning.
**Trigger:** A cross-functional change is assessed without all affected departments and activities being included from the start.
**Impact:** The change must be revised, implementation can be postponed, and the customer and notified body repeat work.
**Workaround:** Transfer change coordination to QMS and use monthly meetings to clarify borderline changes before formal submission.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative quotes:**
> "The mistakes happen mostly due to communication. Because sometimes during a project, for example, during a change, some departments are not included." - P03

> "If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body." - P03

## Possible opportunity
Test a change-impact workflow that makes affected functions, required assessments, and notified-body implications explicit before submission.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Partial platform coverage forces continued email and spreadsheet tracking

**Theme:** [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]
**Description:** The existing app is not used by all actors and covers only a subset of the participant's projects.
**Trigger:** Tracking non-Class III, non-Munich-managed, or Italy-managed activity.
**Impact:** The participant cannot rely on the app as one place to coordinate project status or messages.
**Workaround:** Continue email, phone, and personal Excel tracking.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P01 states the coverage gap directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P01

**Representative quotes:**
> "In this moment it's not work for all the project or for the whole activity." - P01

> "Personally, I don't use this way because, as previously said, not all actors are using this app." - P01

## Possible opportunity
Validate rollout coverage and participant adoption before positioning a platform as an end-to-end communication channel.

frontmatter.name: Request Follow-up Requires External Email
frontmatter.theme: [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Pending requests require email follow-up outside UCI

**Theme:** [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]
**Description:** When an application request is pending, the participant must switch to email because UCI does not let her continue the request conversation in context.
**Trigger:** A submitted request needs a reminder or follow-up.
**Impact:** Follow-up context is split between UCI and email, adding administrative effort and making request history harder to trace.
**Workaround:** Refer to the request number and date in a separate email.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P02 states this directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative quotes:**
> "Ich kann den Request nicht aufgreifen. Das heißt, ich muss auf das E-Mail zurückkommen, um den Request mit der Nummer zum Glück dann aufzugreifen und auch das Datum nochmals aufzugreifen, um das zu reminden." - P02
>
> Translation: "I cannot pick up the request again. That means I have to return to email to pick up the request with its number and date again in order to send a reminder."

## Possible opportunity
Test request-linked messages and reminders that preserve the request number, current status, and conversation history.

**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P12 describes the repeated requests directly, with a concrete example).
**Evidence Note:** All 6 quotes come from the same single interview (P12); this reflects depth of description from one participant, not corroboration across multiple sources — see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count".
**Severity/Confidence risk:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (see Definitions.md); this finding should not be prioritized as if Confidence were High until cross-interview validation confirms it — `needs-validation-before-prioritization` would apply once a second interview is added.
**Description:** The customer repeatedly requests already reviewed supplier evidence because supplier documents cannot be retained internally, may contain competitor-sensitive information, and are reassessed during later reviews.
**Trigger:** A reviewer asks for supplier evidence for a change that depends on a supplier process already reviewed in earlier work, or supplier evidence must be submitted without exposing confidential supplier content to the manufacturer.
**Impact:** Suppliers become frustrated, charge for repeated document requests, and customer response times increase. Manufacturer staff still carry coordination and evidence-quality checks.
**Workaround:** Request documents again from suppliers, coordinate the response outside the certification platform, and sometimes ask suppliers to rework inadequate evidence.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 6
**Interview IDs:** P12

**Representative Quotes:**
> "So what we want, so for instance, if we're submitting, I don't know, a change on packaging or something like that, and you've already assessed the sterility, say, three times before." - P12

> "Our suppliers are getting very frustrated with us requesting the same documents and we're not allowed to hold their documents in our QMS." - P12

> "We've won sterility cycle that's been reviewed 27 times and every time it's had a deficiency even though it's fine." - P12

> "They charge us every time we ask for documents to cost us a fortune." - P12

> "If there was like a Dropbox for suppliers they could use, it would be great because a lot of these, sometimes we have issues where they don't want to share something with us because competitor information is part of it." - P12

> "I mean, we do like to see it sometimes just to make sure, because sometimes, honestly, what they send us isn't good enough. We have to send it back for rework and stuff." - P12

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
Test supplier direct upload, manufacturer-visible completion status, optional manufacturer evidence review, and previously reviewed evidence references that preserve evidence ownership and confidentiality.

**Validation question:** Confirm whether other manufacturers repeatedly request the same supplier evidence because they cannot retain it, because suppliers need confidential upload routes, or because TUV reassesses it for each change.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Submitted application documents are hidden after project creation

**Theme:** [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]
**Description:** Application documents submitted through the service portal are not visible after UCI creates the related project.
**Trigger:** A submitted service request is converted into an active project.
**Impact:** Users must search their own records to verify what they originally submitted, weakening project traceability.
**Workaround:** Retrieve the original documents from internal storage.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview (P08 and P09 both directly report the same disappearance).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P08, P09

**Representative quotes:**
> "Wenn das Projekt angelegt wurde, ich sehe die Antragsunterlagen nicht mehr in U.C.I." - P08
>
> Translation: "When the project has been created, I can no longer see the application documents in UCI."

> "Wenn ich im kompletten Projekt alles drin hab, dass auch jemand, den ich aufs Projekt zugreifen lasse, auch dann die ganzen Application Form sehen kann, was wir beantragt haben." - P09
>
> Translation: "When everything is in the complete project, someone whom I give project access should also be able to see all the application forms showing what we requested."

## Possible opportunity
Preserve submitted request documents as read-only, project-linked records once a request becomes a project.
