notes.body:
# Pain Point: Submitted requests show edit history instead of submission time

**Theme:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
**Description:** A submitted service request shows its last-edited state rather than a clear submission timestamp.
**Trigger:** The customer checks when a service request was transmitted while waiting for TUV follow-up or project creation.
**Impact:** The customer cannot verify the start of the waiting period or answer internal questions about why no response has arrived.
**Workaround:** Reconstruct the submission date from memory or other records.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P09 states this directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P09

**Representative quotes:**
> "Das hab ich auch schon mal angemerkt, dass man da nicht sehen kann, wann der Service Request wirklich übermittelt wurde. Ich glaub, da steht nur 'zuletzt bearbeitet' Stand oder sowas wird angezeigt." - P09
>
> Translation: "I have already pointed out that you cannot see when the service request was actually submitted. I think it only shows a 'last edited' status or something similar."

## Possible opportunity
The request history should show an immutable submitted-at timestamp and acknowledgement alongside later edits.

notes.body:
# Pain Point: UCI notifications cannot be acknowledged without downloading files

**Theme:** [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]]
**Description:** A UCI document notification cannot be acknowledged as read without downloading the document.
**Trigger:** A user sees a document notification that does not require a local download.
**Impact:** Users create unnecessary files and extra actions merely to clear a notification state.
**Workaround:** Download the document even when it is not needed locally.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P10 states this directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P10

**Representative quotes:**
> "Dann sehe ich halt eine Notification. Die kann ich aber heute nicht gefühlt nicht als gelesen aktivieren. Die muss ich mir runterladen. Die will ich aber gar nicht runterladen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Then I see a notification. At present, I do not feel that I can mark it as read. I have to download it, although I do not want to download it."

## Possible opportunity
Users should be able to view and explicitly acknowledge a notification without creating a local document copy.

# Pain Point: Unclear service completion and invoice timing delays administrative closure

**Status:** `Standalone preliminary finding`; not yet a cross-interview theme.
**Validation status:** Needs cross-interview validation before this finding is treated as a pattern.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P01 states the ambiguity directly).
**Severity/Confidence risk:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (see Definitions.md); this finding should not be prioritized as if Confidence were High until cross-interview validation confirms it — `needs-validation-before-prioritization` would apply once a second interview is added.
**Validation question:** Do other customers also lack a clear service-completion and invoice-payment endpoint, and does this delay administrative closure?
**Description:** The completion point of a service and timing of associated invoices are unclear or delayed.
**Trigger:** Technical assessment closes or a certification reaches its final stages.
**Impact:** The accounting department has difficulty closing activities.
**Workaround:** None stated; P01 seeks clarification through contacts.

> "It's not clear for me when the process ends with the service cost invoice payment." - P01

> "There are some delay in our invoice, and then our department, the account department is sometimes very in trouble for close relativity and all that." - P01

# Pain Point: Ungrouped service documents make request history difficult to manage

**Theme:** [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]
**Description:** Documents from multiple service requests can become unmanageable when they are listed together and named inconsistently.
**Trigger:** A request contains multiple services and accumulates documents.
**Impact:** The participant cannot reliably tell which document belongs to which service.
**Workaround:** None stated.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence (P02 states this directly).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative quotes:**
> "Wenn ich dort alle Dokumente gelistet habe, weiß ich nicht mehr, welches zu welchem gehört. Das ist unmöglich." - P02
>
> Translation: "If I have all documents listed there, I no longer know which belongs to which. That is impossible."

## Possible opportunity
Test service-level document grouping and consistent system-generated naming before relying on a combined document list.

frontmatter.name: Digitally Signed Forms Force Print-and-Scan
frontmatter.theme: [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]

notes.body:
# Pain Point: Write-protected TUV forms require print-and-scan workarounds

**Theme:** [[Customers want certification work and documents consolidated in one platform instead of switching channels]]
**Description:** A digitally signed or write-protected TUV form cannot accept required customer information directly, so the customer must use a local PDF or paper workaround before re-signing and returning it.
**Trigger:** A customer needs to add a reference, such as an offer number, to a TUV-signed or write-protected form.
**Impact:** An otherwise digital commercial workflow becomes a manual local-document process and risks transcription, handling, or version errors.
**Workaround:** Print and scan the form, or create a local editable PDF, enter the information, sign it, and upload it again.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview (P10 and P11 both directly report the same print-and-scan workaround).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P10, P11

**Representative quotes:**
> "Das kann ich aber nicht eintragen, weil das PDF digital signiert ist vom TÜV. Das kann ich nicht ändern. Das kann ich aber auch nicht als PDF drucken. Das muss ich ausdrucken und scannen." - P10
>
> Translation: "I cannot enter that because the PDF is digitally signed by TUV. I cannot change it, nor can I print it as a PDF. I have to print and scan it."

> "Eure Quotation ist unterschrieben und schreibgeschutzt. Ich muss mir die runterladen, dann druck ich mir die noch mal ins PDF, damit die nicht mehr schreibgeschutzt ist." - P11
>
> Translation: "Your quotation is signed and write-protected. I have to download it and print it again as a PDF so that it is no longer write-protected."

## Possible opportunity
Replace post-signature PDF annotation with structured customer reference fields and a sequential digital-signature flow.

# Need: Customers need a consolidated view of products, suppliers, sites, and shared data

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Review product families, suppliers, sites, and shared characteristics in a consolidated tabular view.
**Related Theme:** [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]]

## Evidence
> "With this kind of system we cannot have an overview and a summary of all the list of our devices with our devices with a list of all the study barrier sterilization process or main supplier." - P01

> "Wenn man das nicht auf Artikelnummer Ebene eintragen muss, sondern für einen Basic U.D.I., das würde uns natürlich schon sehr helfen." - P09

> Translation: "If data did not have to be entered at article-number level but could instead be managed for a Basic UDI, that would help us greatly."

> "Dass ich ein Dashboard habe, das mir meine Projekte zeigt und ich vielleicht auch so selbst konfigurieren kann oder zusammenziehen kann, wenn wir bei 'Wünsch dir was' sind. notes.body:
# Need: Customers need automatic certification-data checks and reminders for missing information

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Validate certification data automatically and remind accountable users when supplier certificates or required attributes need attention; offer consequential changes as explicit user-confirmed proposals rather than silently applying them.
**Related Theme:** [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]

## Evidence
> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion." - P04
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."

> "Wenn ich das und das eintrage, hat es diese Prüfung zur Ursache, also dass ich dann mache, wenn ich so eingebe, was halt richtig ist oder was falsch ist, also dass ich es selber erkennen kann." - P06
>
> Translation: "If I enter this or that, it causes this assessment, so I should be able to recognize myself whether what I enter is right or wrong."

> "Gibt es dann so eine Art Vorprüfung oder sonst irgendwas? Geht es in die Richtung, wo ich mir wünschen würde, als Kunde vielleicht dazu sagen, ich schicke das einfach mal zum Check ein und es läuft durch und gibt mir dann die formalen Punkte." - P10
>
> Translation: "Could there be some kind of preliminary check? I would like to submit something for a check and have it identify the formal issues."

> "Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut." - P11
>
> Translation: "The AI could say that a related item also needs changing and ask whether it should do that; I could actively choose yes or no, and that would be acceptable or even good."

# Need: Customers need field-level history for shared data changes and review actions

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** See, at field level, who entered, changed, reviewed, or commented on shared certification data, while preserving an approved manufacturer-controlled record.
**Related Theme:** [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]

## Evidence
> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "In der Datenbank könnte ich mir ja gut vorstellen, dass man das über Status abfangen kann. Also Entered by Manufacturer, Reviewed by Notified Body, Feedback by Notified Body oder so." - P07
>
> Translation: "In a database, I could imagine handling this through statuses: entered by manufacturer, reviewed by notified body, feedback by notified body, or similar."

> "Also nachvollziehbar über 'ne Änderungshistorie wäre wichtig, dass man letzten Endes sieht, was ist an dem Datensatz aktuell geändert worden oder was ist in der Änderung und mit welchem Bezug zu einem zu welchem Projekt ist das gerade in der Änderung?" - P09
>
> Translation: "A traceable change history would be important so that one can see what has been changed in the record, what is currently being changed, and which project the change relates to."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

notes.body:
# Need: Customers need scoped roles for viewing and changing certification data

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Assign scoped manufacturer contributor, approver, and notified-body reviewer roles so each party can view or act on certification data without losing ownership or accountability.
**Related Theme:** [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]]

## Evidence
> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht." - P07
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."

> "Was da drin steht, gehört zu uns." - P07
>
> Translation: "What is in it belongs to us."

> "I would prefer to maintain the platform open just to few person in the company." - P03

> "Dann vielleicht auch mit dem Status 'ne klare Abgrenzung, was dürfen wir umsetzen, also welchen Status dürfen wir ändern und welchen Status dürfen wir nicht setzen, also dass wir gar nicht die Möglichkeit haben, vielleicht was auf Covered by Certificate oder Ähnlichem zu setzen, weil das 'ne reine TÜV-Offline wäre." - P09
>
> Translation: "Statuses should clearly distinguish what we may change and what we may not set, so that we cannot set something to 'Covered by Certificate' because that would be solely for TUV."

> "Meiner Meinung nach hat der Hersteller die Datenhoheit, weil es unsere Daten sind." - P10
>
> Translation: "In my opinion, the manufacturer has data sovereignty because they are our data."

> "Wir haben fur die R. A. Mitarbeiter im Prinzip Adminrechte, also die sehen einfach alle Projekte und konnen uberall auch andern und eintragen und Messages schreiben." - P11
>
> Translation: "Our Regulatory Affairs employees essentially have administrator rights: they see all projects and can change, enter, and write messages everywhere."

> "Basically, they don't really need to see our information. The Dropbox is really all they need. Just that they do it and that we could see that it was done without them to see what was done would be great." - P12

notes.body:
# Need: Customers need the required fields and documents for each selected service

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Select the intended service or change scenario and receive the exact required fields, documents, definitions, and examples for that scenario rather than interpreting generic forms or repeatedly asking a contact.
**Related Theme:** [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]

## Evidence
> "Wenn ich jetzt eine Neuproduktanmeldung habe, was brauchen Sie dafür noch mit dazu, reicht da nur die IFQ, wollen Sie da gleich Broschüren haben oder sonstige Informationen?" - P06
>
> Translation: "If I have a new product registration, what else do you need for it? Is the IFQ enough, or do you also want brochures or other information?"

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"

> "Wenn es da noch irgendwie was an die Hand geben könnte, wie so ein Fallbaum. Ich ändere das, ich ändere das." - P09
>
> Translation: "It would help to have something like a decision tree: I change this, I change that."

> "Wenn ich sage, nein, wünscht ihr was, dann habe ich 'ne Plattform, heißt die U.C.I. oder wie auch immer und ich logge mich ein und sage, ich mache 'ne new Application und dann wähle ich aus, will ich jetzt mein Ist es produktbezogen, ist es QM-System bezogen und ich habe eine gewisse Logik dahinter und ich werde dementsprechend durchgeführt." - P10
>
> Translation: "If I could wish for it, I would have a platform where I log in, create a new application, choose whether it concerns a product or the quality-management system, and am guided by the appropriate logic."

> "Sometimes it is confusing if it's QMS or if it's product, where it's, so for a high class change, if it's a design change, I always put in a product change. And then sometimes I get a feedback saying, oh, does GMS change as well?" - P12

> "Wenn ich jetzt bei einem den Eintrag eher fuge einen E. R. C. Code fur diese Seite hinzu und wenn da jetzt ein Icon ware, Information, Achtung, ERC Codes, blablabla, einfach so ein bisschen und ein paar Links, ja klar, ware naturlich immer toll." - P11
>
> Translation: "If I add an ERC code for a site, it would be helpful to have an information icon with guidance and links about ERC codes."

> "So what we want, so for instance, if we're submitting, I don't know, a change on packaging or something like that, and you've already assessed the sterility, say, three times before." - P12

> "And the questionnaire basically is like just a list of your full text file. And it's like, has this changed? Yes. And you give the document number and you submit it." - P12

> "Wir mussen das ja erst mal bei euch anmelden und durfen ja auch nicht implementieren, bevor das approved ist." - P11

# Need: Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** See the timing and current step of the certification process.
**Related Theme:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]

> "I think it will be very important to know the time, to know the step of the certification process." - P01

> "Was man nicht hat, ist den Request Progress." - P02

# Recommendations Register

Recommendations are no longer stored as separate notes. Each recommendation lives inside
its anchor insight in `05_insights` under a `## Recommendation` section. This register is the
single prioritized list for scanning across the whole study. Update a row whenever a
recommendation is added or its priority changes.

| Priority | Recommendation | Anchor Insight |
|---|---|---|
| High | Recommendation 1: Shared product record as the single source, replacing per-certificate spreadsheet copies | [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] |
| High | Recommendation 2: Reduce manual entry volume at intake via bulk import, EUDAMED matching, and Basic UDI reuse | [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] |
| High | Recommendation 3: Governed synchronization for source-system integrations, gated on regulatory approval | [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] |
| High | Recommendation 1: Separate action-required alerts and let users acknowledge without downloading | [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] |
| High | Recommendation 2: Escalate unaddressed actions by project ownership, not access level | [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] |
| High | Recommendation 3: Reduce routine notification volume via email escalation and preference-based digests | [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] |
| High | Recommendation 1: Shared, versioned workflow with defined review steps (entry, TUV review, feedback, resolution, approval) | [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] |
| High | Recommendation 2: Field-level history tied to the version, so feedback and current/superseded state stay visible | [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] |
| High | Recommendation 1: Restrict certification-authority statuses to TUV and default customer master-data access to read-only | [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]] |
| High | Recommendation 2: Traceable, field-level audit trail with customer confirmation before automated changes | [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]] |

notes.slug: _status
notes.path: 05_insights/_status.md
notes.title: Insight Status
notes.body:
# Insight Status

Updated: 2026-08-04

2026-08-11 update: `Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites` was split after a discriminant-validity review found two bundled jobs. The original title/file was kept for the frozen-file/parallel-version reconciliation mechanism (P01, P04, P06, P08, P12). The role/permission/audit-trail mechanism (P07, P09, P10, P11, P12) moved to the new `Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail`. Historical entries below are left as originally written and predate this split; where they cite governance evidence (P09, P10, P11, P12) alongside the old title, the governance-specific evidence now supports the new split insight instead.

- Theme [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]: P10 provides a tenth direct confirmation; frequent revisions and MDR/MDD structure differences force repeated cell-by-cell entry. Linked to [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]].
- Theme [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]: P10 provides an eighth direct confirmation; participants still wait for TUV to consolidate the latest file. Linked to [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]].
- Theme [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]: P10 provides a tenth direct confirmation. UCI is useful after project setup, but customer-led request initiation, task ownership, intermediate milestones, notification acknowledgement, and locked form completion remain incomplete. Linked to [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]].
- PP04 [[Unclear service completion and invoice timing delays administrative closure]]: P02 supplies related pre-quotation evidence only; retain as a standalone preliminary pain point, not a theme or insight.
- Themes [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]] and [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]] (successors to the former combined theme): P10 provides a direct confirmation and adds standardized integration, directly editable records, and automated formal pre-checks; linked to [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] and [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]].
- Theme [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]]: P10 provides a ninth direct confirmation that long-term named contacts remain valuable alongside digital workflows; linked to [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]].
- Theme [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]]: P09 adds related evidence about documents requested during assessment, but does not directly confirm missing pre-quotation cost or module rationale. Counts remain unchanged and no insight is justified.
- PP09 [[Long assessment intervals make submitted change documentation outdated]] and PP10 [[Missing affected departments or assessments cause change resubmission]]: one interview supports each standalone preliminary pain point; no theme or insight is justified yet.

- Theme [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]: P11 provides an eleventh direct confirmation; teams copy one updated Appendix into multiple related projects and the general repository. Linked to [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]].
- Theme [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]: P11 provides a ninth direct confirmation; an open draft still relies on manual highlighting and change history. Linked to [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]].
- Theme [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]: P11 adds related positive evidence that shared UCI project access works; it does not establish a new visibility pain or change counts. Linked to [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]].
- Theme [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]] (successor to the former combined theme): P11 provides a direct confirmation that source synchronization must respect approval gates and automation must wait for explicit confirmation. Linked to [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] and [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]].
- Theme [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]]: P11 provides a tenth direct confirmation that recurring human coordination works well. Linked to [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]].
- Theme [[Customers cannot see quotation costs or assessment-module rationale before acceptance]]: P11 provides related or no direct evidence only; no new insight is justified. PP04 [[Unclear service completion and invoice timing delays administrative closure]], PP09 [[Long assessment intervals make submitted change documentation outdated]], and PP10 [[Missing affected departments or assessments cause change resubmission]] remain standalone preliminary pain points.

[[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]] is supported by direct evidence across eleven interviews and two high-confidence themes. Its embedded recommendation (reuse structured product data across certification records) is listed in [[_recommendations-register]]. [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] is supported by nine direct cross-company confirmations of revision reconciliation plus high-confidence structured-collaboration and manual-maintenance themes; its embedded recommendation (shared records with controlled review, feedback, and approval steps) is listed in [[_recommendations-register]]. [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]] is supported by high-confidence visibility and guidance themes across ten interviews; its embedded recommendation (separate action alerts from routine updates and escalate unaddressed work) is listed in [[_recommendations-register]]. P11 does not justify a new insight or recommendation.

- Theme [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]: P12 provides a twelfth direct confirmation; large affected-SKU changes, supplier changes across multiple appendices, and spreadsheet scale limits strengthen [[Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source]].
- Theme [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]: P12 provides a tenth direct confirmation; master Appendix ABC records can contain current and future states and reviewers may assess old revisions. This strengthens [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]].
- Theme [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]: P12 provides an eleventh direct confirmation; project categorization, bulk access setup, exportable fields, post-review dates, role-specific notifications, and response reminders strengthen [[Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact]].

notes.body:
# Insight: Repeated Appendix ABC entry shows the need for one reusable product-data source

**Insight:** The main problem with Appendix ABC is repeated manual data entry. Customers need one reusable source for shared product data, while keeping the links and fields that are specific to each certificate.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]], [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]], [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]

## Evidence
**Supporting quotes:**
> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information." - P03

> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information." - P01

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export." - P04
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."

> "We have that metadata within, you know, our own systems." - P05

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden." - P06
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise." - P08
>
> Translation: "We cannot simply press a button and tell it to take the data from a particular database on our side and put it into the table in a particular way."

> "Das ist natürlich auch unser Wunsch, dass man 'ne Situation hat, wo man bei uns in der in der Datenbank 'ne Information einträgt und der Datensatz, wenn er dann komplett ist, halt auch transferiert werden kann, so wie das für die Eutermed auch funktioniert, dass man da nichts händisch eintragen muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "Our wish is to enter information in our database and transfer the record once it is complete, as with EUDAMED, so that nothing has to be entered manually."

> "Wenn man das nicht auf Artikelnummer Ebene eintragen muss, sondern für einen Basic U.D.I., das würde uns natürlich schon sehr helfen." - P09
>
> Translation: "If data did not have to be entered at article-number level but could instead be managed for a Basic UDI, that would help us greatly."

> "Wenn jetzt die Schnittstelle ein Standardformat ist, das wäre natürlich sehr gut." - P10
>
> Translation: "If the interface used a standard format, that would naturally be very good."

> "Das bedeutet fur uns, wir mussen diese Excel-Tabelle von Version 21 5 mal in 5 Projekte reinkopieren, funfmal noch mal diese spezifische CN Nummer an die Datei reinschreiben und das dann sechsmal, weil im Generalprojekt ja auch in UCI hochladen." - P11
>
> Translation: "This means we have to copy Excel version 21 into five projects, write the specific CN number into the file five times, and do it a sixth time because it must also be uploaded in UCI in the general project."

> "There's no way for me to filter the appendix for those exact SKU numbers. So I have to go through them one at a time to reference the change on the appendix." - P12

> "I would like if when I'm loading my SKUs up, I can just take ISO, MEDSAP, MDR or whichever. So I don't have to do any duplication." - P12

**Business impact:** Repeated data entry takes measurable time from regulatory and quality teams and increases the risk of conflicting records. P11 reports copying one Excel appendix version into 5 projects, re-entering the same certificate-specific reference number 5 times, and uploading it a 6th time to the general project in UCI ("Universal Customer Interface") for a single change. This repeated-entry cost recurs on every device-portfolio change, even when customers already keep the underlying product data in structured systems or manage very large Appendix ABC portfolios.
**Design implication:** Effective solutions should use shared, structured records instead of separate spreadsheet copies. They should reuse matching data from the European Database on Medical Devices (EUDAMED), support Basic Unique Device Identifier (UDI) reuse, support bulk import across related schemes, and guide users through certificate-specific fields. They should support integrations and bulk imports, check data before submission, and synchronize changes only after regulatory approval.

## Recommendation
The design implications above cover at least three separately shippable and testable product decisions. Each should be scoped, prioritized, and tested on its own rather than shipped as a single bundled feature.

**Recommendation 1 — Shared product record as the single source:** Certificate views should read from one shared, structured product record instead of separate spreadsheet copies per certificate. Links between devices, sites, suppliers, and schemes should let a single update propagate everywhere it applies, removing the P11-style repeat-and-reupload pattern.
**Recommendation 2 — Reduce manual entry volume at intake:** The workflow should support bulk import, matching data from the European Database on Medical Devices (EUDAMED), and reuse at Basic Unique Device Identifier (UDI) level where possible. Users should receive guided entry only for the remaining certificate-specific fields that cannot be sourced this way.
**Recommendation 3 — Governed synchronization for source-system integrations:** Customers with structured source systems should get a documented export or integration path. Source-system changes should synchronize into the shared record only after regulatory approval, so automated intake does not bypass review.
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]], [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]], [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]], [[Large changing device portfolios make Appendix ABC maintenance labor-intensive]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce repeated updates, duplicate entry, and conflicting certification records.
**Risk:** EUDAMED does not contain every certificate-specific field, and some customer data still sit in documents. P12 confirms that supplier, sterility, certificate, and linkage fields may remain outside UDI systems and may need confidential supplier-side contribution. Mappings, timing, access, approval, and ownership should be validated before a source is treated as authoritative. Recommendations 1-3 should still be sequenced and validated together, since Recommendation 1's data model constrains what Recommendations 2 and 3 can reuse.
**Priority:** High

_2026-08-11: Refined per review feedback. Removed the P05 "synchronization issues" quote (coded `#code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision`; moved to [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]], its correct code-matched theme). Business impact now cites the P11 quote as explicit time-cost evidence instead of an unsupported generic claim. Recommendation split from one bundled list into 3 separately scoped/testable recommendations; register updated accordingly._

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.
This recommendation is listed in [[_recommendations-register]].

notes.body:
# Insight: Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites

**Insight:** Shared data will not remove rework if a version is frozen for review while the customer keeps changing it in parallel. The shared record needs review-lifecycle steps tied to the version itself, so neither party's parallel edits are silently overwritten or lost.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]], [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]

_2026-08-11: Split from the original bundled insight after a discriminant-validity review found two distinguishable jobs: reconciling frozen file versions with parallel edits (process-timing, kept here) and controlling who may change shared data with a traceable history (governance/control, split into [[Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail]])._

## Evidence
**Supporting quotes:**
> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon." - P04
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

> "The master contains both the old one and the future state, which is a bit confusing for everybody involved." - P12

**Business impact:** Manual reconciliation between a frozen file and a parallel customer edit takes time and can lose reviewer feedback, leaving conflicting certification records.
**Design implication:** Effective solutions should use a shared, versioned workflow with distinct steps: manufacturer entry, TÜV review, feedback, resolution, and approval. The workflow should keep field-level comments and history tied to the shared version, so feedback is not lost and the current vs. superseded state stays visible instead of requiring manual re-merging.

## Recommendation
The design implications above cover two separately scoped/testable product decisions.

**Recommendation 1 — Shared, versioned workflow with defined review steps:** The workflow should replace exchanged review files with one shared, versioned certification record carrying defined steps (manufacturer entry, TÜV review, feedback, resolution, approval), so parallel edits reconcile through the record instead of manual re-merging.
**Recommendation 2 — Field-level history tied to the version:** Field-level comments and version history should stay attached to the shared record, so reviewer feedback and the current vs. superseded state remain visible across frozen and continuing versions.
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]], [[Concurrent reviewer files require manual feedback realignment]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce manual comparison and re-entry between frozen and continuing versions, and prevent lost reviewer feedback.
**Risk:** The workflow must distinguish important certification changes from low-risk corrections so review steps do not slow down minor edits.
**Priority:** High

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.
This recommendation is listed in [[_recommendations-register]].

notes.body:
# Insight: Shared certification data needs role-scoped permissions and a traceable audit trail

**Insight:** Customers need control over who may change shared certification data and a traceable record of what changed. Without scoped permissions, defined statuses, and confirmation before automated updates, customers cannot trust that shared data reflects an approved, accountable state.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]], [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]

_2026-08-11: Split from [[Shared certification data needs review steps that prevent silent overwrites]] after a discriminant-validity review found two distinguishable jobs bundled together: reconciling frozen file versions with parallel edits (process-timing, kept under the original insight) and controlling who may change shared data with a traceable history (governance/control, this insight)._

## Evidence
**Supporting quotes:**
> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Dann vielleicht auch mit dem Status 'ne klare Abgrenzung, was dürfen wir umsetzen, also welchen Status dürfen wir ändern und welchen Status dürfen wir nicht setzen, also dass wir gar nicht die Möglichkeit haben, vielleicht was auf Covered by Certificate oder Ähnlichem zu setzen, weil das 'ne reine TÜV-Offline wäre." - P09
>
> Translation: "Statuses should clearly distinguish what we may change and what we may not set, so that we cannot set something to 'Covered by Certificate' because that would be solely for TUV."

> "Also nachvollziehbar über 'ne Änderungshistorie wäre wichtig, dass man letzten Endes sieht, was ist an dem Datensatz aktuell geändert worden oder was ist in der Änderung und mit welchem Bezug zu einem zu welchem Projekt ist das gerade in der Änderung?" - P09
>
> Translation: "A traceable change history would be important so that one can see what has been changed in the record, what is currently being changed, and which project the change relates to."

> "Dann unter Umständen, wenn es unsere Daten sind, dann vielleicht irgendeine Acknowledgement-Genehmigung oder sonst irgendwas." - P10
>
> Translation: "When it is our data, there should perhaps be some acknowledgement or approval."

> "Da ware es naturlich auch cool, wenn das im neuen System zwecks Traceability auch einfach ruckverfolgbar ist, also welche Changes zu dem jeweiligen Produkt bei welchem Feld passiert sind und ahnliches." - P11
>
> Translation: "It would be good if the new system made traceability straightforward, showing which changes happened to each product and field."

> "Dass die K. I. dann sagt, hey, du hast hier gerade das geandert, dann musste man aber auch das, soll ich das fur dich machen und ich dann aber aktiv ja oder nein drucken kann, dann das ware noch O. K., wenn nicht sogar gut." - P11
>
> Translation: "The AI could say that a related item also needs changing and ask whether it should do that; I could actively choose yes or no, and that would be acceptable or even good."

> "I would like the appendix to be a read only document for me." - P12

**Business impact:** Teams spend effort proving where a change came from and avoiding unauthorized master-data edits. Without scoped statuses, customers or TUV could set or change certification-authority states that neither party is accountable for.
**Design implication:** Effective solutions should give TUV exclusive control over certification-authority statuses, keep a field-level, traceable audit trail of who changed what, request customer acknowledgement or confirmation before material or automated changes take effect, and make customer access to master certification data read-only where a direct edit would imply an unapproved change.

## Recommendation
The design implications above cover two separately scoped/testable product decisions.

**Recommendation 1 — Restrict certification-authority statuses and default to read-only master data:** Only TUV should be able to set certification-authority statuses (for example "Covered by Certificate"). Customer access to shared master certification data should default to read-only where a direct edit would imply an unapproved change.
**Recommendation 2 — Traceable audit trail with confirmation before automated changes:** The record should keep a field-level, traceable audit trail of who changed what and when. Automated or related-record updates should require explicit customer confirmation before they are applied.
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]], [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce unauthorized or unaccountable changes to shared certification data and reduce the effort customers spend tracing who made a change.
**Risk:** Confirmation prompts on every automated change risk alert fatigue if not scoped by materiality; read-only master-data access must not block customers from submitting an actual change request.
**Priority:** High

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.
This recommendation is listed in [[_recommendations-register]].

notes.path: 05_insights/Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact.md
notes.title: Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact
notes.body:
# Insight: Status tools need actionable alerts and access to a responsible contact

**Insight:** Status tools help only when people can clearly see what needs action and can quickly reach a person for complex questions. Missed alerts or a system-only process can delay work.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]], [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]], [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]]

_2026-08-11: the prior single visibility theme was split into three narrower successor themes. This insight now draws on the timing/ownership successor and the new notification-routing successor; the platform/channel-consolidation successor is not a supporting theme here._

## Evidence
**Supporting quotes:**
> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "Ich kenn es schon aus der Vergangenheit bei anderen Unternehmen, wenn ich von den Systemen so viele Bling und Bings und hier ist was geschehen und hier ist was geschehen, dann habe ich also schon mehrfach überlegt, da gibt es so 'n Overflow und was passiert, keiner erfasst die Sachen mehr, weil es zu viel Bling, Bling und Bing und Bang ist." - P06
>
> Translation: "I know from the past at other companies that when systems produce so many pings and notifications that something happened, there is an overflow and nobody notices things anymore because there is too much pinging."

> "Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich überhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss." - P09
>
> Translation: "I receive at least 20 notifications per week that do not concern me. But I am an administrator because I also need to manage project-specific access."

> "Ich finde, wir sind eigentlich schon ziemlich gut in der Kommunikation, jetzt insbesondere durch U.C.I. die [unser TUV-Kontakt] als zentrale Ansprechpartnerin, also da dauert es keinen halben Tag, hat man 'ne Antwort oder zumindest, ich hab's weitergegeben, ich kümmere mich drum." - P09
>
> Translation: "I think communication is already quite good, especially through UCI and [our TUV contact] as the central contact; it takes less than half a day to receive an answer or at least confirmation that it has been forwarded and will be handled."

> "Ich möchte meinen Project Handler oder meinen Relationship Manager, wie auch immer, rein. Nicht dass ich zuerst durch muss und sitz dann wie gefühlt die 10 Minuten in der Warteschlange." - P10
>
> Translation: "I want to bring in my project handler or relationship manager, rather than first having to go through a process and wait in a queue for ten minutes."

> "If we had your response is due in two days, I would love if that went to everyone who owned your project." - P12

> "I would like if we could separate technical questions from project management questions." - P12

> "Dann sehe ich halt eine Notification. Die kann ich aber heute nicht gefühlt nicht als gelesen aktivieren. Die muss ich mir runterladen. Die will ich aber gar nicht runterladen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Then I see a notification. At present, I do not feel that I can mark it as read. I have to download it, although I do not want to download it."

**Business impact:** When people miss a question, reviews take longer: P05 reports realizing the presence of a question "a week or two late." When status is unclear, both customers and TUV spend time chasing updates. Broad project access can also send messages to people who are not accountable for the task, as P09 reports receiving roughly 20 irrelevant notifications per week solely because of an administrator role.
**Design implication:** Effective designs should show acknowledged alerts for required actions and provide a direct, project-linked route to a responsible contact. Users should be able to mark notifications as read without downloading files. Alerts should remain separate from access rights. Project-, role-, and task-based preferences should reduce routine notification volume.

## Recommendation
The design implications above cover at least three separately scoped/testable product decisions.

**Recommendation 1 — Separate action-required alerts and let users acknowledge without downloading:** The notification model should separate actions that need a response from routine updates. Users should be able to mark a notification as read without downloading a file.
**Recommendation 2 — Escalate by ownership, not access level:** Unaddressed actions should escalate through a direct, project-linked route to the responsible TÜV contact. Alerts should route based on project ownership or task responsibility, not viewing or administrator rights.
**Recommendation 3 — Reduce routine notification volume:** Email should support urgent escalation. Project-, role-, and task-based preferences and digest summaries should reduce routine notification volume.
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]], [[Undifferentiated notification settings cause customers to miss critical alerts or receive irrelevant ones]], [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]], [[Deficiency notifications without email alerts can remain unseen for weeks]], [[Coupled access and notification settings send administrators irrelevant alerts]], [[UCI notifications cannot be acknowledged without downloading files]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce missed deficiencies and status-chasing while keeping the personal support people need for complex questions.
**Risk:** Alert severity, recipients, timing, and escalation rules need tuning to avoid notification fatigue.
**Priority:** High

_2026-08-11: Recommendation split into 3 separately testable items (acknowledgement, ownership-based escalation, volume control). Added the P10 quote grounding the "acknowledge without downloading" claim, which previously appeared only in Design Implication/Recommendation without direct evidence. Business Impact updated to cite the P05 "week or two late" and P09 "20 irrelevant notifications" quotes as concrete evidence. All six Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points are now directly evidenced within this insight's own Evidence section._

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.
This recommendation is listed in [[_recommendations-register]].

Und da bekomme ich in der Woche bestimmt 20 Mitteilungen, die mich überhaupt nicht betreffen. Ich bin aber Administrator, weil ich auch projektbezogene Zugriffe regeln muss.

notes.body:
# Positive Pattern: Named TUV contacts clarify required certification information

**Theme:** [[Named auditor contacts help customers prepare required certification information]]
**Process phase:** Request/Application; Change; Review
**Description:** Named TUV contacts provide document lists and regular meetings that clarify what is needed before and during certification work.
**Why it works:** Participants know whom to contact, receive actionable information requests, and can resolve borderline questions before formal submission.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A digital workflow could remove useful tailored guidance if it offers only generic forms or help.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 14
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07, P09, P10, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "With [our auditor], we are quite well informed about the information needed." - P01

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity." - P01

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen." - P02
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "Wir haben 'nen ungefähr 'nen monatlichen Call, wo aber dann auch Quality Sterility Assurance dabei ist, wo unsere offenen Themen besprochen werden." - P04
>
> Translation: "We have an approximately monthly call that also includes Quality and Sterility Assurance, where our open topics are discussed."

> "We have a weekly meeting with our project handler and coordinator." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung." - P06
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut." - P07
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."

> "Ich finde, wir sind eigentlich schon ziemlich gut in der Kommunikation, jetzt insbesondere durch U.C.I. die [unser TUV-Kontakt] als zentrale Ansprechpartnerin, also da dauert es keinen halben Tag, hat man 'ne Antwort oder zumindest, ich hab's weitergegeben, ich kümmere mich drum." - P09
>
> Translation: "I think communication is already quite good, especially through UCI and [our TUV contact] as the central contact; it takes less than half a day to receive an answer or at least confirmation that it has been forwarded and will be handled."

> "Das funktioniert aber eigentlich auch gut, da haben wir auch die Vereinbarung, wir sagten, wann die Listen quasi eingefroren sind, dann gehen die an den [unser TUV-Kontakt], der zieht die, migriert die mit einem Migration Tool oder irgendwas und dann kriegen wir sie wieder zur Verfügung gestellt und haben dann das neue Template verwendet mit den Daten aus der vorherigen Version." - P09
>
> Translation: "This actually works well: we agree when the lists are frozen, they go to [our TUV contact], he migrates them with a migration tool, and we receive the new template containing the data from the previous version."

> "Das sind ja so Situationen, wo wir mit [unserem TUV-Kontakt] dann sprechen. Wir arbeiten im [unserem TUV-Kontakt] ja schon, wie gesagt, seit keine Ahnung, also sind es 8 Jahre, 10 Jahre irgendwie so was zusammen. Und ich glaube auch, dass das wir gut mit ihm reden können und irgendwie eine Frage ist, dann hilft er uns jedes Mal und dann ist es halt auch für uns jetzt halt einfach, er ist ein vertrauter Kontakt, dem kann man was fragen." - P10
>
> Translation: "Those are situations where we speak with [our TUV contact]. We have worked with him for eight or ten years, can talk to him well, and whenever there is a question, he helps us; he is simply a trusted contact whom we can ask."

> "So I meet with [our project handlers] like once a week." - P12

> "I usually give them a heads up verbally first and then submit it on UCI." - P12

## Update note
Confidence remains High. P12 adds a tenth direct confirmation that regular named contact helps customers prepare and schedule change submissions.

notes.body:
# Positive Pattern: TUV-managed template migration prevents manual Appendix rebuilding

**Theme:** [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]
**Process phase:** Change
**Description:** The customer and TUV agree a time to pause changes. A named TUV contact then moves the existing Appendix data into the new template and returns it.
**Why it works:** A clear handoff and tool-supported migration prevent the customer from manually rebuilding the new template.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** Customers could have to rebuild the new template themselves. Keep the migration support, but avoid a long editing lock or competing versions.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview (P09 and P11 both directly describe this practice working well).

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P09, P11

**Representative quotes:**
> "Das funktioniert aber eigentlich auch gut, da haben wir auch die Vereinbarung, wir sagten, wann die Listen quasi eingefroren sind, dann gehen die an den [unser TUV-Kontakt], der zieht die, migriert die mit einem Migration Tool oder irgendwas und dann kriegen wir sie wieder zur Verfügung gestellt und haben dann das neue Template verwendet mit den Daten aus der vorherigen Version." - P09
>
> Translation: "This actually works well: we agree when the lists are frozen, they go to [our TUV contact], he migrates them with a migration tool, and we receive the new template containing the data from the previous version."

> "Da haben wir dann aber von euch ein Update bekommen, wo alle Daten schon migriert waren. Also das war naturlich unheimlich toll." - P11
>
> Translation: "We received an update from you in which all data had already been migrated. That was naturally extremely good."

## Update note
Confidence: Low -> Medium, P11 added an independent confirmation that TÜV-provided migration reduces customer manual effort.

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b.

notes.body:
# Positive Pattern: UCI keeps active project requests, messages, and documents together

**Theme:** [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
**Process phase:** Request/Application; Review
**Description:** UCI keeps electronic requests, project communication, and active-project documents in one place for these participants.
**Why it works:** Stakeholders can use a common project location instead of relying only on email recipients and individual inboxes.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A redesigned workflow could lose useful project communication and document context while fixing the handoff from request to project.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 5
**Interview IDs:** P08, P09, P11, P12

**Representative quotes:**
> "Mit U.C.I. hat sich schon einiges verbessert, weil man da tatsächlich ja elektronisch diese Anträge stellen kann, dann auch zu diesen Projekten dann immer alles an einer Stelle in der Kommunikation und auch von den Projektdokumenten her hat." - P08
>
> Translation: "UCI has already improved quite a lot because applications can be submitted electronically and the communication and project documents are then all in one place for those projects."

> "Ansonsten, ja sonst, wenn die Projektplanung dann steht und die ganzen Module, wie [unser TUV-Kontakt] eben auch gesagt hat und das alles geplant ist, dann funktioniert das da ab für folgendes Tracking und Planen sehr gut und da haben wir tatsächlich nicht noch zusätzlich im Hintergrund bei uns auf unserer Seite Tools." - P09
>
> Translation: "Once the project plan and all the modules are set up, tracking and planning work very well from that point onward, and we do not use additional tools in the background on our side."

> "U. C. I. ist in dem Fall sehr gut, weil einfach alle Zugriff haben." - P11
>
> Translation: "UCI is very good in this case because everyone has access."

> "UCI, I mean, it's gotten very positive feedback. We really like it." - P12

> "What I love about UCI is the history. I've got all my projects there open and closed." - P12

## Update note
Confidence remains High. P12 adds a fourth direct confirmation that UCI centralizes active and closed project history and reduces email dependency.

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b.

# Proto-segments

| Interview ID | Suspected Segment | Key Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Regulatory and quality assurance lead at a medical-device manufacturer | Primary contact with the certification body; manages a large, changing device portfolio; relies on Excel, ERP, technical documentation, and auditor guidance. |
| P02 | Regulatory Affairs Manager at a medical-device manufacturer | Primary certification contact and sole UCI user; consolidates technical documentation from subject-matter experts; maintains live Appendix ABC data and project/cost tracking in Excel. |
| P03 | Quality Management System Manager at a medical-device manufacturer | ISO 13485 management representative; owns QMS changes, audits, and quality-system communication; jointly maintains Appendix ABC with Regulatory Affairs. |
| P04 | Regulatory Affairs specialists at a large medical-device manufacturer | Coordinate notified-body applications and Appendix ABC across a large product portfolio; rely on SAP, Teamcenter, SharePoint, and cross-functional coordination. |
| P05 | Regulatory Affairs managers at a large medical-device manufacturer | Manage MDR remediation, Class III maintenance, renewals, and high-volume Appendix ABC data; rely on project-handler relationships, email, and partially adopted UCI workflows. |
| P06 | Regulatory Affairs leaders at a medical-device manufacturer | Manage MDR and MDSAP Appendix ABC records across global registrations; coordinate controlled document versions, PLM and external data, UCI submissions, and management-level project reporting. |
| P07 | Quality Management System lead at a medical-device manufacturer | Manages QMS applications, audits, certificates, and QMS changes; coordinates with Regulatory Affairs on controlled Appendix records, multiple data systems, and notified-body review. |
| P08 | Cross-functional certification stakeholders at a large medical-device manufacturer | Includes Quality Management, Audit Management, Regulatory Affairs authority management, and Regulatory Affairs labeling/data management; collectively maintain high-volume Appendix ABC data and coordinate UCI projects. |
| P09 | Cross-functional Regulatory Affairs and Global Quality Management team at a large medical-device manufacturer | Regulatory Affairs owns product files and Appendix data for about 120 devices; Global Quality Management coordinates TUV communication, distributed project access, and high-volume UCI tracking. |
| P10 | Senior Quality Management leaders at a global medical-device manufacturer | Direct Quality Management leaders coordinate notified-body communication, significant changes, audits, commercial approvals, distributed data, and strategic quality-system digitalization. |
| P11 | Regulatory Affairs team at a medical-device manufacturer | Maintains Appendix ABC across multiple product groups, coordinates approval-gated supplier and product changes, and manages shared UCI project work with controlled team access. |
| P12 | Associate director for European regulatory strategy at a large medical-device manufacturer | Central TUV contact for a large trauma portfolio; manages changes, submissions, Appendix ABC updates, supplier evidence, UCI project access, and internal timeline communication. |

A proto-persona has been created in `07_personas`: [[Regulatory certification lead managing product data and notified-body work]], supported by P01, P02, P04, P05, P06, P11, and P12. P12 directly confirms central notified-body contact, product-file ownership, Appendix maintenance, supplier evidence coordination, and certification-data governance. Persona splitting check after P10: P03, P07, and P10 are three role-specific QMS interviews with a consistent goal of governing audits, certificates, QMS changes, and notified-body coordination. Their responsibilities differ fundamentally from Regulatory Certification Leads' product-file and data-ownership focus, so [[Quality Management certification lead coordinating audits and certification changes]] is created as a separate proto-persona. P08 and P09 remain mixed-role evidence of cross-functional collaboration rather than homogeneous support for either persona.

# Persona: Quality Management certification lead coordinating audits and certification changes

**Segment:** Quality Management certification lead at a medical-device manufacturer
**Based on interviews:** [[P03]], [[P07]], [[P10]]

## Context
Coordinates quality-management changes, audits, certificates, and communication with TUV. Connects Regulatory Affairs, Quality Management, operations, and external stakeholders while keeping a clear record across UCI, internal systems, shared files, and direct contact.

P10 shows that senior Quality Management leaders may also oversee significant changes, commercial approvals, global quality operations, and digitalization. They need a portfolio view but still need clear tasks, deadlines, and certification messages.

## Goals
- The persona needs audits, certificates, significant changes, and related actions to remain traceable without reconstructing context across systems.
- The persona needs a clear view of current ownership, deadlines, and outstanding certification work.
- The persona needs access to notified-body experts while reducing document, email, and spreadsheet administration.

- [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]

- [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]
- [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]
- [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]]

## Associated pain points
- [[Customers cannot see timing or current status between certification steps]]
- [[Customers cannot create UCI requests before TUV creates a project]]
- [[UCI notifications cannot be acknowledged without downloading files]]
- [[Write-protected TUV forms require print-and-scan workarounds]]

## Associated needs

- [[Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step]]
- [[Customers need to acknowledge notifications without downloading documents]]
- [[Customers need the required fields and documents for each selected service]]

# Persona: Regulatory certification lead managing product data and notified-body work

**Segment:** Regulatory certification lead at a medical-device manufacturer
**Based on interviews:** [[P01]], [[P02]], [[P04]], [[P05]], [[P06]], [[P11]], [[P12]]

## Context
Coordinates certification submissions with TUV, gathers technical and product data from internal systems and experts, and keeps Appendix ABC evidence ready for changes and audits. Uses email, meetings, spreadsheets, and internal product-data systems to keep work moving.

P05 shows that this role may manage MDR remediation, Class III maintenance, and renewals across large portfolios, using direct contact when the platform view is incomplete.

P06 shows that Regulatory Affairs leaders manage controlled Appendix ABC versions, gather data from PLM and other sources, and report team status to management.

P11 shows that Regulatory Affairs teams coordinate open Appendix drafts across product groups, apply approval gates before source-data changes enter certification records, and want automation to ask before it acts.

P12 shows that this role can act as the central notified-body contact for all changes and submissions, administer UCI access at scale, coordinate supplier evidence, and explain TUV timing internally.

## Goals
- The persona needs complete, traceable certification changes without repeated data entry or reconciliation.
- The persona needs a reliable current state across internal product data, Appendix ABC, EUDAMED, and notified-body work.
- The persona needs request status, timing, and change references without reconstructing them from emails and separate trackers.

## Associated themes
- [[Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual assembly from multiple internal sources]]
- [[Frozen Appendix ABC files require manual alignment with continuing customer work]]
- [[Customers cannot reliably see timing or progress between certification stages]]
- [[Customers need reusable, bulk data entry instead of repeating fields per certificate]]
- [[Customers prefer data channels ranging from Excel upload to system-to-system integration]]
- [[Customers need role-based governance and audit trails over shared certification data]]
- [[Customers want portfolio-level visibility into their certification data]]

## Associated pain points
- [[Large changing device portfolios make Appendix ABC maintenance labor-intensive]]
- [[Concurrent reviewer files require manual feedback realignment]]
- [[Fixed Appendix rows require separate reference lists]]
- [[Customer change-notification IDs are lost across TUV correspondence and billing]]
- [[Deficiency notifications without email alerts can remain unseen for weeks]]
- [[Bulk project teams must be added one project at a time]]
- [[Repeated Supplier Evidence Requests Increase Response Cost]]

## Associated needs
- [[Customers need to edit product, site, supplier, and relationship records directly]]
- [[Customers need their change-notification ID retained through the TUV process]]
- [[Customers need automatic certification-data checks and reminders for missing information]]
- [[Customers need dependable alerts when deficiency questions require a response]]
- [[Customers need the required fields and documents for each selected service]]
- [[Customers need confirmation when TUV receives or reviews a submission]]
- [[Customers need to approve consequential certification-data updates before application]]
- [[Customers need project notifications independent of access permissions]]
- [[Customers need to see certification timing and the current process step]]
